* Experience with ERP and planning tools (e.g., Oracle, NetSuite, Adaptive) preferred

description:
**About Rebar**
---------------

Rebar is building the AI operating system for commercial HVAC, Electrical, and Plumbing.

Over the past year, our quoting platform has processed tens of thousands of projects across North America, and we’ve doubled our revenue in the first 6 weeks of this year. Our customers include many of the top firms in the industry. Some of these companies are running billion-dollar construction projects on workflows that still look like it’s 1985.

Construction is 10% of GDP and still massively underserved by software. We are changing that.

Rebar is redefining how the construction industry operates with innovative, AI-native products built for the trades. Backed by top investors and entering our next phase of growth, we’re looking for our Founding Talent Partner to help build the world-class team that gets us there.

**Job Overview**

We’re not just looking for a recruiter; we’re looking for a strategic talent partner who will revolutionize how we scale our talent function. You’ll own the complete hiring cycle, from strategic sourcing and outreach through pipeline development to candidate close. Attracting top talent is the single biggest lever in this next stage of growth. This is a highly visible role where you are the face shaping our future team’s experience through every critical touchpoint.

**What You’ll Do**

* Drive High-Volume Hiring: Execute full-cycle recruitment across a high volume of open roles, balancing technical AI/software engineering positions with specialized construction and operations talent.
* Aggressive Sourcing: Proactively hunt passive candidates through LinkedIn, GitHub, JuiceBox, niche tech communities, and construction networks to keep our pipelines constantly full.
* Partner with Leadership: Move fast alongside our founders and department leads to scope out roles, set realistic timelines, and adjust strategies on the fly.
* Own Candidate Experience: Deliver a transparent, fast-moving interview process that keeps candidates engaged and excited about our vision, even in a highly competitive market.
* Optimize Startup Tech Stack: Manage candidate flow using our Applicant Tracking System (ATS), ensuring pristine data integrity while keeping the hiring loop moving daily.
* Build the Employer Brand: Act as the first point of contact for the company, pitching our mission to disrupt a massive legacy industry using cutting-edge AI.
* Own hiring end to end. You run intake with the hiring managers, source and screen candidates, manage the loop, and close offers. You are accountable for whether we hire the right people on time.
* Run our agency partners. Set search priorities, coordinate day-to-day, and hold agencies accountable to quality and speed. You decide which searches we run ourselves and which go to agencies, based on cost, urgency, and how hard the role is to fill.
* Build the pipeline before we need it. Outbound sourcing, referrals, and networks, so the next opening starts with warm candidates instead of a blank page.
* Design a process that scales. Scorecards, structured interviews, and hiring manager training, so every loop is consistent, and every decision is grounded in evidence.
* Measure it. Own our ATS and recruiting data. Report on pipeline health, agency performance, and time to hire, and use it to fix what is slowing us down.
* Set the bar. Shape how Rebar shows up to candidates, from job descriptions to the final call, and partner with leadership on headcount planning and compensation benchmarking. As recruiting grows here, you are the natural person to lead it.

**What You Bring**

* 4+ years of proven experience in talent acquisition, ideally within a fast-scaling tech startup, a fast-paced agency, or a high-volume hiring environment.
* Dual-Track Sourcing: Ability to switch contexts effortlessly between technical roles (AI/ML engineers, full-stack developers), Product Managers, GTM, and construction or operations-focused positions.
* Sourcing Grit: Proven track record of finding creative ways to source top talent beyond standard job board postings, adopting new, innovative, AI-native, and unique sourcing techniques.
* Execution & Velocity: High comfort level with ambiguity, rapid changes in hiring priorities, and the fast-paced nature of a Series A environment.
* Communication: Exceptional storytelling skills with the ability to clearly explain a complex technical vision to candidates.

**Compensation & Benefits**

* Competitive salary based on experience
* Equity: meaningful grant, aligned with your background
* Benefits: medical, dental, vision
* Perks: free lunches and dinners

This is a full-time, on-site role in NYC’s Flatiron District, steps from Madison Square Park and Union Square.

title: Content Creator & Strategist, Social
description:
**Who We Are**

Tomo is a digital mortgage company on a mission to eliminate the greed and complexity in lending, helping homebuyers save thousands of dollars. Our AI-driven customer experience makes the lending process faster, less frustrating, and more affordable. By passing these savings directly to homebuyers, we eliminate excessive fees and inflated rates that cost Americans billions each year. Backed by top-tier venture investors, including Ribbit, Citi Ventures, NFX and Progressive Insurance, Tomo is poised to become one of the most valuable fintech startups of our generation.

**About the Role**
------------------

We’re seeking a hands-on content creator and strategist who loves fast experiments and makes decisions from data. You know that great content is part art and part science. You pair creative instinct with analytical rigor to build a content engine that grows an audience and drives real business results.

This role is focused on one thing: building Tomo’s organic social into a channel that earns attention, builds brand awareness, and drives conversion over time. Mortgages are one of the biggest financial decisions people make, and we want Tomo to be the brand they already know and trust when it’s time to make it.

You’ll own the execution and optimization of Tomo’s organic social channels, from concept to camera to analytics. Then you’ll read the data, work out why something landed (or didn’t), and make the next one better.

This is a hands-on creative role where you’ll be both in front of the camera and behind it, filming yourself and our team (sales, ops, leadership, etc.) to create content that grows our audience and drives measurable results.

You’ll work closely with the Senior Director of Growth Marketing, who sets the overall marketing, growth, and brand strategy, and alongside peer GMMs owning paid media and organic search.

**What You’ll Do**
------------------

**Content Creation & Production**

* Concept, script, film, and edit a high volume of short-form video and static posts across social platforms such as TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, and LinkedIn.
* Appear on camera yourself, and cast and direct the Tomo team so our content is never just one face. Partner with teammates to source stories, customer questions, and on-camera talent.
* Write hooks, scripts, captions, and on-screen copy that make mortgage concepts worth watching and engaging with.
* Support the AEO/SEO GMM on long-form YouTube production, from filming and editing to cutting long-form into short-form clips.

**Channel Strategy & Formats**

* Execute and evolve Tomo’s organic social strategy: content pillars, series, the content calendar, and platform-specific approaches.
* Pitch, prove out, and scale repeatable formats and series built to travel beyond Tomo’s followers: content people share and remix, not just like.
* Track trends, sounds, and formats in real time across personal finance, real estate, and internet culture. Turn them into on-brand content fast, and know when a trend is already over.

**Analytics & Experimentation**

* Own organic social KPIs such as reach, hook rate, watch time, saves and shares, follower growth, and the site traffic and leads that come from social. Reporting should come with clear, data-backed recommendations.
* Run structured creative tests such as hooks, formats, length, talent, and posting cadence, and keep what you learn in a living playbook.
* Connect content performance to brand awareness and funnel conversion metrics, not just in-platform performance.

**Brand, Community & Compliance**

* Represent Tomo’s voice in public, with good judgment on tone, timing, and risk.
* Work within our review process. Mortgage-related content goes through internal and compliance review before posting, since we’re a regulated lender. Build workflows that keep speed high without cutting corners.
* Manage community engagement across comments and DMs.

**Qualifications**
------------------
**Required**
* 2+ years creating short-form social content for a brand, a client, or your own following. Freelance work and strong personal projects count.
* A portfolio with breakthrough content and measurable virality. We want to see the spike, not just the steady line.
* Comfortable on camera and behind it. You film on a phone or camera and edit your own work in CapCut, Premiere Pro, or similar.
* Comfortable directing others on camera, including people who’ve never filmed before.
 [...] * Experience producing or editing long-form YouTube content.
**Who You Are**
---------------
* Obsessed with measurable outcomes. You turn data into instinct, and instinct into data.
* Biased toward shipping. You’d rather post, learn, and iterate than polish a deck.
* Customer-obsessed. You want to get inside the head of a first-time homebuyer and make content that makes their life easier.
* Really curious about personal finance and home buying. It doesn’t have to be your background, but the interest has to be real.
* Coachable. You’ll cut your favorite joke if it isn’t working and still hit the deadline.
* Entrepreneurial. You spot opportunities, prioritize ruthlessly, and get things done with minimal hand-holding.
* Highly organized. You can run multiple series, shoots, and review cycles at once without dropping threads.
* You make AI work for you to raise output quality and efficiency, without losing your creative judgment.
* A collaborative teammate who’s as comfortable directing a VP as a Loan Advisor.
**Employee Benefits**
We strive to anticipate your needs in order for you to be a healthy, motivated, and happy team member. We provide a variety of competitive benefits including (but not limited to):
* Equity Ownership: All teammates receive stock options—we win together
* Comprehensive Medical, Dental, and Vision plans for you and your dependents with some plans 100% covered
 [...] Compensation Range: $75K

description:
Link Logistics Real Estate (“Link”) is a leading operator of warehouses and business parks, specializing in last-mile logistics real estate. Established by Blackstone in 2019, the company connects consumption, technology, and the supply chain across its portfolio, which spans half a billion square feet. We leverage our scale, proprietary data and insights, and foundational focus on sustainability to drive success for our customers’ businesses and deliver value for our stakeholders. We put our people, customers, and communities first and find ways to make a conscious, positive impact where we live and work. Every day, we work to reinvent and lead our industry forward by thinking bigger and challenging the status quo.

We're hiring a hybrid **ML/Backend Engineer** to own the intelligence layer of Link's Analytics Engine. This is the connective tissue role: you'll design the pipelines that bring disparate real estate data to life, build the knowledge graphs and retrieval systems that make that data queryable by LLMs, and architect the backend services that surface insights to investment teams in real time.

You won't be handed a spec. You'll talk to investment analysts and asset managers, identify where analytical leverage is lost today, and build systems that close that gap — often combining classical ML, graph-based reasoning, and LLM-native workflows in the same solution.

**RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Knowledge Graph & Retrieval — Design graph-based data structures encoding relationships across markets, assets, tenants, and transactions. Build retrieval pipelines (RAG, hybrid search, structured queries) that give LLMs accurate, contextually rich grounding.
* LLM Workflow Automation — Develop rule-based and agentic LLM workflows that automate investment analytical tasks. Own prompt engineering, eval frameworks, and production reliability.
* Data Pipelines — Build ETL/ELT workflows that ingest, normalize, and enrich large-scale internal and third-party datasets (property records, leasing data, macro signals, alt data). Every dataset should have a clear owner, update cadence, and quality SLA.
* Data Trust & Provenance — Build systems that make data trustworthy by design: lineage tracking from source to insight, confidence scoring on derived outputs, and clear attribution so analysts always know where a number came from and how fresh it is. Treat a bad comp or stale signal as a production incident.
* Backend API Layer — Develop and maintain APIs and services that expose ML outputs and structured data to front-end applications. Prioritize low-latency, reliability, and clean contracts with the application team.
* Collaboration — Work directly with investment and asset management teams to understand analytical needs and iterate quickly. Treat analyst trust as a first-class product requirement.

**QUALIFICATIONS:**

* 4+ years in ML engineering, backend engineering, or a role spanning both
* Hands-on experience shipping LLM-powered applications in production — RAG pipelines, prompt engineering, eval frameworks
* Strong Python skills; comfortable owning backend services and APIs end-to-end
* Experience with knowledge graphs or graph databases (Neo4j or similar)
* Proficiency building data pipelines at scale (Spark, Databricks, or equivalent)
* Deep sensitivity to data provenance — a track record of building systems that create analyst trust, not just claim it

Basis builds real agents that do real work in the real economy. Our agents operate for hours at a time, performing end-to-end work for some of the largest accounting firms in the world.

*"Basis is on the frontier of building production-grade, long-horizon agents.
**They've pushed the limits of what we thought our models could do**
on real-world, economically valuable, complex accounting tasks. They've been a great collaborator in helping us shape what the future of agents looks like." — Prashant Mital, Applied AI Lead, OpenAI*
Why finance matters here
  
  
Most finance roles inherit a business model. This one helps build one.
  
  
Our agents do work that accounting firms have always staffed with people. That makes the questions finance owns at Basis the questions that decide whether the company works: how you price hours of autonomous work, what margins look like when compute is a real cost of revenue, how far ahead of demand you build capacity, and where the next dollar of a fundraise should go. There is no playbook for this yet. You’ll help write it.
  
  
If you’ve spent years in banking, private equity, or venture modeling businesses like this from the outside, this is the chance to do it from the inside, with the data, the operators, and the ability to change the answer.
  
  
What you’ll do
  
  
This is not a reporting role. You’ll own the analysis end to end: framing the question, finding the truth in the numbers, deciding what it means, and then making sure the business acts on it. You’ll report to the Head of Finance and work across finance, revenue operations, go-to-market, product, and engineering.
  
  

* Own the models the company runs on. Revenue, headcount, unit economics, cash. Leadership makes decisions off your work, so it has to be right and it has to be legible.
* Take analysis to action. Evaluating a pricing change or a new investment is half the job. The other half is getting the right people aligned and making sure the decision actually gets implemented. You follow the number until something changes because of it.
* Chase down what doesn’t add up. When a metric moves and the explanation doesn’t sniff right, you go deep enough to find out why, whether that’s the data, the contract, or the Slack thread, and you come back with a real answer.

At Morning Brew Inc., we mix what you need to know with our unique brand of wit to attract, and build real relationships with, the next generation of business leaders. We speak to them like people, ensuring they get the context and insight needed to make decisions every day. Loyalty and trust are our most valuable currencies.

Whether scrolling, reading, watching, or listening, our audience trusts us for credible, entertaining business content that makes an impact on their personal and professional lives.

The Morning Brew team is clever, creative, and growing fast. Want in? Read on.

OVERVIEW

Founder Brew, a publication dedicated to exploring the real lives, decisions, and psychology of people building companies — from startups to small businesses to creative ventures—is looking for a reporter to cover the operational truths of being a founder.

Founder Brew explores what it’s like building a business—across startups, small businesses, and “unsexy” real-world companies—and is a publication focused on how current and aspiring founders can be better equipped to handle what comes their way.

Reporting is pragmatically optimistic, and divided between two modes: as-told-to, and traditional reporting. We publish the messy middle, resist PR gloss, and verify the facts behind first-person stories.

We’re looking for a reporter to ideate, research, and create journalism to help take this vertical to new heights.

**WHAT YOU'LL DO**

* Pitch, report, and write 3-5 stories per week for Founder Brew.

* Generate ideas for and lead/co-lead creation of non-newsletter editorial initiatives, enterprise pieces, and evergreen content, as we build out a digital home.

* Conduct research to support creation of key stories and inform longer-term projects.

* Create multimedia components that bring our stories to life in video and audio formats

* When needed, represent Founder Brew at live events, with the possibility of on-stage participation.

* Interest and expertise in business writing and reporting

* At least 3 years of journalism experience

* Ability to write in the Morning Brew style (engaging, informative, clever)

* Ability to quickly source up

* Understanding of how to analyze and draw conclusions from structured and unstructured data

* Understanding of how to leverage multiple platforms (email, social media, etc.) to engage with the target audience

* Self-starter attitude with ability to operate in a collaborative, quickly-changing environment

* Ability to operate in a high-pressure environment with tight deadlines

**BRIEF BREW HISTORY**

Morning Brew Inc. was founded in 2015 by two entrepreneurial college students who noticed their peers were not consuming legacy media resources about business and finance news, but had a high desire to learn about those topics. In 2020 a majority stake in MBI was acquired by Axel Springer SE and in February 2025 that position was increased to full ownership of the business. Axel Springer SE is a family-owned, transatlantic media company headquartered in Berlin and New York that is committed to the values of a free and informed society. title: Screening & Transaction Monitoring Associate
description:

Brex is the intelligent finance platform that enables companies to spend smarter and move faster in more than 200 markets. By combining global corporate cards and banking with intuitive spend management, bill pay, and travel software, Brex enables founders and finance teams to accelerate operations, gain real-time visibility, and control spend effortlessly. Brex's AI-native automation and world-class service eliminate manual expense and accounting tasks for customers so they can focus on what matters most. Tens of thousands of the world's best companies run on Brex, including DoorDash, Coinbase, Robinhood, Zoom, Plaid, Reddit, and SeatGeek.

Working at Brex allows you to push your limits, challenge the status quo, and collaborate with some of the brightest minds in the industry. We're committed to building a diverse team and inclusive culture and believe your potential should only be limited by how big you can dream. We make this a reality by empowering you with the tools, resources, and support you need to grow your career.

**Compliance**

The Compliance team helps the company grow responsibility, advocating for Brex and for the thousands of growing businesses we serve. We own the compliance policies for Brex, provide strategic advice and guidance to all Brex teams, protect Brex from Financial Crime and other compliance risks, and represent the company externally on key regulatory and policy issues. Reimagining the financial system in a highly regulated environment requires creativity and resourcefulness, and we welcome the challenge.

**What you'll do**

As the Screening & Transaction Monitoring Associate, you will review and escalate potential sanctions matches and politically exposed persons (PEPs) hits across our customers, payments, and vendors. You will review and assess screening data to make sound match decisions and assess the sanctions risk each alert poses. Clear communication is essential for documenting match dispositions, writing escalation memos, and discussing potential sanctions exposure with senior management. Experience working with external financial partners, auditors, and regulators is valuable. Adaptability is crucial, as sanctions programs, designations, and geopolitical risk can change overnight, as is keeping a positive, collaborative mindset while managing a high volume of alerts.

**Where you'll work**  
This role will be based in our New York City office. We are a hybrid environment that combines the energy and connections of being in the office with the benefits and flexibility of working from home. We currently require a minimum of three coordinated days in the office per week, Monday, Wednesday and Thursday. As a perk, we also have up to four weeks per year of fully remote work!

**Responsibilities**

* Review and disposition customer, payment, and vendor screening alerts against OFAC, UN, EU, UK, and other applicable sanctions lists, escalating true matches and potential violations
* Conduct PEP reviews, including enhanced due diligence on high-risk relationships
* Take ownership of the effectiveness of our screening controls, spotting, scoping, and driving improvements to workflows
* Assist with the preparation of required sanctions reports, such as OFAC blocked and rejected transaction reports
* Monitor sanctions program changes and new designations
* Support screening vendor integrations and answer questions from L1 alert reviewers
* Help reduce screening false positive rates without weakening coverage
* Help develop and deliver internal sanctions and Financial Crimes training
* Take ownership of the success of our internal controls, spot, scope, and drive opportunities for improvement

**Requirements**

* 4+ years of experience across a variety of financial risk operations (Sanctions, PEP, AML, SAR, BSA, 314a, Watchlist, 314b, Third Party Payment Processing, Fraud, Bribery/Corruption, Due Diligence, etc)
* Strong knowledge of US sanctions programs and OFAC regulations and relevant US financial regulations authorities (ex: FinCEN, FINRA, BIS, etc.)
* Experience with OFAC reporting requirements and timelines, including blocked and rejected transaction reports and voluntary self-disclosures
* Experience with escalating to and communicating with OFAC, banking partners, law enforcement, or other regulators
* Ability to analyze complex ownership structures and money movement across payment methods to identify sanctions exposure
* Familiarity with data analytics tools (SQL, Looker, Snowflake, Hex, Excel), including designing, debugging, and organizing data for a wide audience
* Experience with ComplyAdvantage or similar screening platforms and Unit 21
* Demonstrated ability to work as part of a cross-functional, multi-disciplinary team (Operations, Customer Experience, Legal, Engineering, Product Management, Data) in designing operational work-streams and internal controls

**Bonus points**

* Insatiable curiosity
* Eagerness to learn
* Detail oriented
* Desire to build

**Compensation**  
The expected salary range for this role is $111,197 - $138,996. However, the starting base pay will depend on a number of factors including the candidate's location, skills, experience, market demands, and internal pay parity. Depending on the position offered, equity and other forms of compensation may be provided as part of a total compensation package.

About the New York City Board of Correction
  
  
The New York City Board of Correction (BOC) is a nine-person, non-judicial oversight board, which regulates, monitors, and inspects the correctional facilities of the City. * Establish and ensure compliance with minimum standards “for the care, custody, correction, treatment, supervision, and discipline of all persons held or confined under the jurisdiction of the Department of Correction”
* Investigate serious incidents

NYC Department of Finance (DOF) is responsible for administering the tax revenue laws of the city fairly, efficiently, and transparently to instill public confidence and encourage compliance while providing exceptional customer service.
  
  
DOF’s Administration and Planning Division is responsible for managing and overseeing administrative and operational services for the agency. This includes the daily management of the Offices of Financial Management, Purchasing and Contracts, Operational Services, and Diversity and Inclusion.
  
  
The Office of Employee Services (OES) is responsible for the agency’s human capital administration and workforce management, which includes recruitment, personnel, civil service administration, labor relations, timekeeping, payroll, leaves of absence, benefits and performance management administration, and programs for employee learning, engagement, recognition, professional development, and agency-wide events.

title: Associate General Counsel
description:
Overview:

NRDC (the Natural Resources Defense Council) works to safeguard the Earth, its people, its plants and animals, and the natural systems on which all life depends. NRDC combines the power of more than 3 million members and online activists with the expertise of some 800 policy advocates, lawyers, scientists, and communication experts to confront the climate crisis, protect nature, ensure the rights of all people to clean air, clean water, and healthy communities. As an international nonprofit environmental organization, NRDC is working to address the world’s most urgent environmental challenges, and advance innovative, science-based, and enforceable solutions.

Since our founding in 1970, NRDC has helped craft and deliver many of America’s foundational environmental laws, including the Clean Air Act, Clean Water Act and Safe Drinking Water Act. Today, we continue to lead in advancing and defending strong environmental protections at the local, state, federal and international levels, as well as through the marketplace. Our team works across the United States and around the world, from offices in Chicago, Denver, Los Angeles, New York City, San Francisco, and Washington, D.C., as well as in Beijing, London, and New Delhi (a subsidiary of NRDC India Pvt. Ltd.).

Supported by our members and online activists, NRDC is driving impactful solutions that confront the climate crisis, defend nature and safeguard public health across Asia, Africa, and the Americas. At NRDC, we believe lasting change happens when people bring their talent, passion, and expertise together for a common purpose: to build a cleaner, healthier, and more resilient world. Learn more at nrdc.org.

NRDC is seeking a knowledgeable and motivated Associate General Counsel to work with the General Counsel team in our Washington, DC, Chicago, IL, New York, NY, Santa Monica, CA or San Francisco, CA office.

Position Summary

The General Counsel team provides in-house legal support to all institutional programs and departments. This position will focus primarily (but not exclusively) on providing support for the institution’s advocacy efforts and compliance with federal, state, and local lobbying, and will work in close partnership with colleagues from External Affairs and Programs.

Responsibilities:

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the following essential functions:

* Provide in-house legal support for federal, state, and local lobbying and advocacy initiatives, including advising clients on applicable registration and disclosure rules, gift and ethics restrictions, and ballot measure regulations.
* Advise the NRDC Action Fund, NRDC’s 501(c)(4) affiliate, on federal, state, and local election law matters.
* Modernize and manage NRDC and the NRDC Action Fund’s processes for tracking and reporting lobbying-related time and expenses, in coordination with OGC administrative and outside counsel teams.
* Review incoming and outgoing grants and contracts for compliance with disclosure regimes.
* Provide staff legal training on lobbying, gifts/ethics, political law, and other related issues.
* Provide ongoing legal support on a wide variety of matters to NRDC/AF programs and departments, including support for substantive programmatic and communications work and support for administrative functions (accounting and finance, facilities, human resources, development and IT).
* Assist with the implementation and management of various internal policies.
* Monitor and advise on legal and regulatory developments relevant to NRDC’s operations.
* Work with outside compliance counsel as necessary and effectively manage related billing and budgetary considerations.

The above list of duties is not comprehensive but generally demonstrates the types of matters under this position’s responsibility. Other duties may be assigned.
Qualifications:
Minimum Education & Experience
* Law degree from an accredited law school
* 4-7 years of related experience, with at least 5 years as a lawyer in relevant area.
* Experience with campaign finance and lobbying laws at the federal, state, and local levels.
* Management and/or development of internal lobbying compliance systems
* And/or equivalent education or experience
Skills, Abilities, Competencies
* Substantive knowledge or experience with the Foreign Agents Registration Act, exempt organization regulations, and c3/c4 operations and governance are preferred.
* Development of processes to record and report lobbying activity.
* Communicate complex legal concepts clearly and succinctly, including to lay audiences, in both formal training and informal advising.
* Excellent drafting, research, and written and oral communication skills.
* Strong critical thinking and analytical ability, sound judgment, strategic orientation, and interpersonal maturity.
* Ability to work efficiently in a fast-paced environment, simultaneously handle multiple assignments and meet deadlines independently and with strong attention to detail.
* Integrity, professional discretion and ability to handle sensitive/confidential matters.
* Flexibility and ability to work well independently on multiple projects with a wide variety of people, at all levels of the organization.
* Non-legal experience with advocacy or political organizations is a plus.
* Competence with and commitment to diversity and inclusion; ability to be an effective partner with diverse colleagues, leaders and partners.
* Ability to travel to NRDC U.S. based offices as needed, approximately 15-20%
* Commitment to NRDC’s mission, values, and DEI principles

- Manage day-to-day client relationships and deliver high-quality reports and presentations on schedule.
- Collaborate with senior leaders and sector experts across the BRG Energy & Climate practice.
- Build and strengthen client relationships through effective engagement delivery and ongoing communication.
 Qualifications 
- A bachelor’s degree in Economics, Finance, Accounting, Business, Engineering, or a related field is required. A master’s degree in a related field is preferred.

 PGIM is seeking an Analyst or Associate, Data Analytics & Governance to join our Global Business Enablement team within Real Estate. This role supports two closely connected priorities: delivering trusted data products and analytics that inform decisions across the real estate investment lifecycle, and putting into practice the data governance that keeps that information accurate, well-defined and reusable.
 Working alongside other team members, business stakeholders, data stewards and Technology partners, the Analyst/Associate will document business requirements, trace data back to its sources, catalog and define data elements, and build, monitor and report on data quality rules.  Data Analytics

 Data Governance

PostHog is your product’s context layer. It ingests and stores your analytics, errors, replays, and business data so you and your agents can query and act on it.

We're focused on building an awesome product for end users, hiring exceptional teammates, shipping fast, and being as weird as possible https://posthog.com/deskhog. 

 


THINGS WE CARE ABOUT

 - Transparency: Everyone can read about our roadmap, how we pay (or even let go of) people, our strategy, and how we work, in our public company handbook https://posthog.com/handbook. Internally, we share revenue, notes and slides from board meetings, and fundraising plans, so everyone has the context they need to make good decisions.

BUILDING THE MOST TRUSTED INTERFACE OF HEALTHCARE

We are in the business of trust.

We're designing for the most emotionally charged moments of our customers' lives; the bar isn't just delight, it's trust. Hera's brand promise is simple: care worthy of our parents. This promise is our moat.

It's what physicians refer to, families buy, what Heroes deliver, and what the product must unlock and enforce at every touchpoint.




OUR PRODUCT CHALLENGE 

The bottleneck isn't demand, it's supply. There aren't enough experts to serve every family who needs us. To scale to all of America, we have to unbundle expertise from the human so that anyone who can foster human connection can become a Hero. 

The problem is that this expertise is tribal knowledge. One social worker knows how to expedite Medicaid in New York, another knows which home-visiting PT families actually love. It's trapped in people's heads.  

To solve this,  our platform captures every interaction and turns it into compounding intelligence that makes every user smarter. Think Waymo: expert humans do the driving today, and every mile they log trains the system so that tomorrow, anyone — even with zero healthcare background — can perform like a 20-year veteran. The hard part is building a system that knows what to trust, what's gone stale, what's local versus universal, and how to surface the right insight at the right moment. Get it right and you've scaled healthcare expertise beyond the lucky few who know the right person.

We wrote more on why and how we are building this technology here. https://hellohera.notion.site/what-endures-when-execution-is-free




OUR FOUNDING TEAM

We are in person in NYC. Read our story and watch our launch video here https://hellohera.com/about.







JOIN US TO BUILD OUR STRATEGIC FINANCE FUNCTION

At most companies, finance is a reporting function: close the books, build the budget, explain the variance. This role is different; it is not an FP&A role. At Hera, you're in the room for every big investment we make, and you own the math behind it. Every Hero we hire, every market we open, every payer we contract with and every program we bill under is a bet with a cost and a return that either compounds or doesn’t. You’ll turn those bets into numbers we trust, then go out and move the numbers.

 - Model and link 3-statement borrower financials, amortization schedules, payment-in-kind (PIK) interest, dynamic cash sweeps, DSCR, and debt covenants (Credit track).
   
    

 - Structure bond pricing, yield curves, and fixed income portfolio construction models from the ground up (Debt track).
   
    

 - Review, debug, and improve model accuracy by identifying incorrect assumptions, broken logic, and structural risks.
   
    

 - Clearly explain financial logic, decision-making, and why a model works in structured English.

THIS ROLE IS / THIS ROLE IS NOT

description:

To learn more, visit www.industriousoffice.com/careers http://www.industriousoffice.com/careers.



About the Role

Industrious signs new landlord partnerships every year, and the number is growing as our business development team expands. Before any of those deals move forward, someone has to check that it holds together: that the assumptions are sound, that the start date, budgets, rent, pricing, and returns all track, and that the figures from design and construction have carried through correctly. As a Real Estate Associate on our Real Estate Transactions team that will be your job!



You will underwrite assigned deals in Excel, explain what drives their returns, and flag where a deal is tight, whether on pricing, occupancy, or CapEx. Our business development colleagues make the call on whether a deal goes ahead, and your analysis is what they rely on to make it well. You will work with Design, Construction, Finance, and other teams to make sure every number is right, supporting several business development colleagues as deal flow shifts.



Our approach to underwriting is different from a traditional real estate shop, and we will teach it to you. In your first few months you will get close review and clear guidance while you learn how we work. You will also join at a good time: the team is growing, new roles are being added, and we are underwriting a new product, so there is real room to learn, ask questions, and grow with us.



Success here means accurate work. The team trusts your numbers, your flags are clear, and any mistake you make happens once, not twice.



What Might Your Day Look Like

Your morning starts with a new deal from one of our business development colleagues. You go through the model piece by piece: the start date, the budget, the rent and revenue share assumptions, the cash flows, the IRR, and the margin the location is expected to earn per rentable square foot. The returns look fine at first, but pricing is tighter than it seems, so you note it clearly with the number that would need to change.



Late morning, updated figures arrive from Design and Construction. You check that they have flowed into the model correctly. One CapEx figure does not match the construction budget, so you confirm the right number with the construction team before it goes any further.



In the afternoon, you walk your business development colleague through the deal: what the returns look like, where the risk sits, and which assumptions matter most. They decide what happens next. Then priorities shift, and another colleague needs support on a deal heading to Investment Committee, so you move over and check that every figure in the review material ties back to the underwriting.



Before you wrap up, you update your trackers and checklists so the team knows where every deal you are supporting stands.



What You Will Own

 - Underwrite assigned deals in Excel, checking every assumption and making sure each component, from start date and budgets to pricing and IRR, tracks.
 - Explain each deal's returns clearly, including IRR, cash flows, P&L, and margin, so business development can make an informed decision.
 - Flag where a deal is tight, on pricing, occupancy, CapEx, OpEx, rent, or revenue share, and where it may need more support.
 - Make sure figures from Design, Construction, and Finance carry through accurately into the deal.
 - Support deal reviews and Investment Committee materials with numbers that hold up to scrutiny.
 - Support several business development colleagues across their deal flow, moving between priorities as needs change.
 - Keep the trackers and checklists that help the team stay accurate as deal volume grows.
You Will Love This Role If...
 - You are curious about real estate and want to understand why a deal works, not just what the model says.
 [...]  - Nice to have: exposure to leases, landlords, or office and flexible workspace, and progress toward a designation such as the CFA or CPA. You do not need Argus or prior knowledge of our underwriting approach.
Compensation & Benefits
The base salary for this role is $110,000 - $120,000, depending on experience, skills, and role alignment. This role is also eligible for an annual bonus and participation in our long-term incentive program. But compensation is only part of the story.

 What You Will Do 
 Clinical Spend Forecasting 
 ●     Build and own the clinical trial forecast by vendor, study and cost category (CRO services, pass through costs, site grants, lab, technology, imaging, IRB). 
 ●     Hold a regular dialogue with Clinical Operations to capture changes as they happen: enrollment pace, site activation, protocol amendments, scope changes and timeline shifts. 
 ●     Translate each trial change into its cost and timing impact, and keep forecasts and estimates on the latest plan, not the one in the original contract. 
 ●     Produce the clinical inputs to the annual budget, quarterly reforecasts and cash runway models. 
 Vendor Spend and Invoice Review 
 ●     Maintain a tracker for every clinical vendor that matches each invoice line to its MSA, SOW, work order and executed change orders, and tracks remaining contract value by category. 
 ●     Support the clinical AP process: track incoming invoices in our AP platform, tie them to their POs and study, catch duplicates, and route them to Clinical Operations for review. 
 ●     Review vendor billing by hours, units, milestones and pass through costs against the contract and real study progress, and flag resource use that looks out of scope, overstaffed or ahead of the work before invoices are approved. 
 ●     Track CRO prefunded deposits and site grant funds: what has been prepaid, applied and credited back. 
 ●     Keep a running exceptions log and escalate each item for resolution with the vendor or a Pathos decision.

 ●     Close the loop each month: compare invoiced and accrued spend to forecast by vendor and category, and explain the variances. 
 ●     Keep the clinical spend dashboard current and reconciled to Pathos billing and accounting platforms. 
 ●     Prepare monthly spend, burn and variance reporting for the SVP of Finance and Clinical Operations leadership. 
 Clinical Procurement 
 ●     Support the finance side of contracting: review SOW and change order budgets, compare pricing and rate cards to prior work, flag issues for the SVP of Finance, and confirm budget availability before signature. 
 ●     Provide vendor, study and budget details for purchase order setup in Bill.com. 
 Clinical Accruals 
 ●     Prepare the monthly clinical accrual for each vendor, built from vendor reported work, unit and milestone data, site activity and Clinical Operations input, for review by the SVP of Finance. 
 ●     Maintain accrual and prepaid schedules that support the accounting team’s journal entries and reclasses, and reconcile them to subsequent invoices. 
 ●     Support the annual audit and investor diligence with clear, documented clinical expense support. 
 Who You Are 
 Required Qualifications

 ●     2 to 4 years as a financial analyst at a biotech, pharma company or CRO, with direct exposure to R&D or clinical trial costs across multiple studies. 
 ●     Working knowledge of how clinical trials are contracted and billed: MSAs, SOWs, change orders, pass through costs, site payments and prefunded deposits. 
 ●     Experience building forecasts and variance analyses. 
 ●     Understanding of accrual accounting and month end close. You can build an accrual from operational data with documented support. 
 ●     Advanced Excel: you build models others can follow, audit and update. 
 ●     A strong interest in using AI tools and automation in daily work, with examples of workflows you have streamlined or rebuilt to cut manual effort and errors. 
 ●     The confidence to question a vendor invoice and the judgment to work collaboratively with Clinical Operations. 
 Preferred Qualifications 
 ●     Hands on clinical accrual ownership for one or more studies. 
 ●     Experience with QuickBooks Online and Bill.com, or similar ERP and AP tools. 
 ●     Exposure to oncology trials. 
 ●     Experience on a small finance team where you covered several roles. 
 ●     CPA progress or MBA coursework. 
 What Success Looks Like 
 In your first year: 
 ●     Within 90 days, every active vendor has a current tracker reconciled to its contract, the GL and the spend dashboard. 
 ●     No overrun reaches an invoice unflagged, and trial changes show up in the forecast and accruals the same month. 
 ●     Clinical accruals close each month with documented support and no material true ups at audit. 
 Location 
 This is a hybrid role based in our New York City office, with in-person attendance on Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays. 
 Drug development shouldn’t be guesswork, not when patients are waiting. 
 Pathos is building a next-generation biotech with AI at the core. Not as a feature, but as the operating system for how medicines get developed. MISSION

Neko Health is a health technology company that opened its first clinic in Stockholm in 2018, founded by Daniel Ek and Hjalmar Nilsonne.

description:

Minerva builds AI for marketing leaders. We work together with marketers to automate and accelerate their workflows with AI agents. Our agents augment the end-to-end workflow of the marketer by automating analysis, campaign planning, activation, measurement and reporting.

Customers like the NBA, Ramp, Wander, Hard Rock Stadium Group and Luxury Presence use Minerva to develop a better understanding of their customers and introduce AI specifically built to understand the customer into their commercial organizations. Our campaigns outperform other tools because we built the entire stack: from identity to enrichment to data integration as well as agents to action and report on the analysis.

Our team brings together operators and investors from Citadel, Dentsu, Bridgewater, Meta Superintelligence, Growthloop, Amazon and Lazard, alongside engineers and researchers from Berkeley, MIT, Stanford and Cambridge.


ABOUT THE ROLE

You’re Minerva’s first strategic finance hire. You have maximum exposure to the key business bottlenecks that the executive team grapples with on a day to day basis. Ideally you’re able to identify and take the first pass on solving many of these problems.

You sit within the operations org and work with the CEO, Chief-of-Staff, VP of Ops and broader leadership team to prioritize analyses. You prepare models that help guide capital allocation and real resource allocation.

This is a generalist role with broad scope - spanning planning, operations, go-to-market, pricing, board and investor reporting and special projects.

 - Own the core financial models that guide capital allocation and resource planning.

 - Design incentive systems that improve employee performance, retention and satisfaction.

 - Design commercial policies (pricing, packaging, contract terms) that deeply align our incentives with our customers while building a sound financial foundation across products.

 - Optimize A/P and A/R policies with Accounting / RevOps.

 - Partner with CoS to own all board, investor, and internal reporting materials, turning complex data into clear narratives that drive decisions.

 - Work with the CEO & CoS to develop operating KPIs and reporting systems.

 - Build business cases for strategic decisions including deal structuring, investments, hiring plans, and product launches.


IDEAL QUALIFICATIONS

 - Extreme agency, candor and rigor

 - 4-7+ years of experience in strategic finance, investment banking, private equity, growth equity, or a similar high-rigor analytical role

 - Corporate development exposure is a plus but is not required.

 - Strong financial modeling skills and the ability to build complex operating models from scratch, including experience with unit economics and cost structure analysis

 - Comfort with ambiguity and a bias toward ownership

 - Willingness to match or outpace the hours and intensity of the leadership team

 - More likely to answer a question by finding the person who has already solved the problem than deriving an answer from first principles

 - Willingness to have an opinion and share it

 - Enthusiasm for AI and Minerva’s mission


COMPENSATION

Base salary: $175,000–$300,000, depending on seniority. Significant equity exposure.


HOW TO APPLY

Skip the cover letter. Send us one model you built and the decision it changed: the question, how you structured it, the answer and what happened. If the model is confidential, describe the structure.


WHERE WE WORK

We work in person from our office at 300 Kent Avenue in Williamsburg, Brooklyn.

1) Improving accessibility and quality of healthcare is something we live and breathe. Everyone on Camber’s team cares deeply about helping clinicians and patients.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Camber is hiring an Enterprise Strategy Associate to partner with our Director of Enterprise Revenue to build the narrative behind our largest client partnerships. Revenue cycle is the bloodline of a clinic, and through data, you build trust with the client. You will drive the narrative that helps a clinic understand the impact Camber can have on its business, and you’ll use it to shape the strategy of the deal.

This is not a traditional analyst role. You will follow a clinic through its entire time at Camber, from the first conversation to a fully rolled-out partnership, and keep driving the value of Camber at every step. You will join a team that values agency, intellectual honesty, and a “rowing in the same direction” mentality.

Your time will be split across three stages of the client journey:

 - Go-to-Market: You leverage a clinic’s data to build the narrative for how Camber can impact its revenue cycle, partnering with a Director of Enterprise Revenue on the analysis and story to win the deal.

 - Implementation: You are the subject-matter expert on both Camber and the clinic, and that expertise drives how we serve them. You help make sure the value of Camber is seen and understood as we roll out.

title: Revenue Operations Lead
description:
ABOUT HARPER

Harper is an AI-native commercial insurance brokerage for small businesses. We built our own software for nearly every step, so our people spend their time where trust matters. We use AI to earn that trust.

Our AI writes notes, enriches leads, and routes work all day. You own the revenue system underneath it, and you make it tell the truth.

Two dashboards disagree about last week's close rate. You trace it to a stage that changed without its owner changing, fix the definition, add a test to the routing rule, and publish one number. The next Monday the forecast moves, and this time everyone can see why.

At most growing companies, RevOps gets pieced together: a routing rule here, a dashboard there. That got Harper to roughly 100x growth. It will not get us through the next stage across three offices.





WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the funnel definitions. Give every revenue stage one meaning, one entry and exit rule, one source, and one owner.

 - Own CRM behavior and routing. Every field, automation, and routing change has a test case, an owner, an effective date, and a rollback path.

 - Own the forecast. Publish the method, inputs, and assumptions, and reconcile the variance to booked revenue every cycle.

 - Instrument revenue. Make demand, contact, intake, quote, close, bind, and booked revenue reconcile to their source records.

 - Turn analysis into action. Find where volume, conversion, speed, or handoffs break, and give the fix a named owner.

 - Automate with controls. Use AI for enrichment, notes, tasks, and reporting only when the source and correction path stay visible.




WHAT YOU NEED

 - You have owned revenue, sales, or growth operations at a fast-growing company. This is the background we have been missing.

 - You understand CRM architecture, lifecycle stages, routing, attribution, and forecasting from the inside, and you can write SQL or test a claim in the data yourself.

 - You want to be measured on booked revenue and conversion, not dashboard activity, and you say so plainly when a change did not work.

Insurance experience helps, and it is not required. If you meet most of this, apply.




THE REALITY: READ THIS BEFORE YOU APPLY

This job starts as archaeology. You will find every definition that drifted and every automation nobody owns, and fix them while revenue keeps moving. There is no pause button and no clean handoff.

This is not the seat if you want to administer a CRM without owning the outcome, if you produce reports but not recommendations, if you want to run sales management or marketing creative, or if you need a remote or hybrid schedule.

It is the seat if building one revenue system everyone trusts sounds like the work you want.




HOW WE HIRE

 1. A 30-minute team call on Zoom.

 2. An office session of about two hours, meeting more of the team and working a real problem with us.

 3. A superday in the office, showing how you operate in real time. We decide after this.



The basics

 - Pay: $160,000 to $210,000 base. Bonus and equity eligible.

 - Where: On-site, five days a week, in the room with the team, with travel to Atlanta and New York. San Francisco at 425 Market Street.

 - Hours:  5am to 7pm PT, Monday through Friday.

 - License: None required.

 - Benefits: Health, dental, and vision. San Francisco adds three meals a day in the office, commuter benefits, and a gym membership.




HOW TO APPLY

Send your resume and a short note about a funnel or CRM problem that looked like a data issue but was really an operating issue. Tell us how you proved it, what you changed, and the result.




EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER

Harper is an equal opportunity employer. We consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

 Sparkfund prices and structures its Distributed Capacity Procurement deals using a set of programmatic pricing models, and this role is responsible for both sides of that work: building the ad hoc project finance models a deal needs when it falls outside the existing templates, and keeping the standing programmatic models accurate as cost, revenue, timing, and financing assumptions shift. You'll work from our existing model library, but you'll also be expected to build new models from scratch when a deal structure calls for something the templates don't cover. 
 The work sits between Finance and the teams closest to the deals. You will partner with Business Development, Program, and Project teams to source the assumptions that feed a model, test them against the underlying data, and flag anything that doesn't hold up before it reaches a pricing output. You will also translate model output into language deal teams can use when they negotiate. You will report to the Director of Corporate Finance. - Build, audit, and maintain the programmatic pricing models used to structure and price deals across Sparkfund's DCP programs

- Strong attention to detail and comfort validating assumptions across multiple sources
- Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to translate model output for people who don't work in finance
- Bachelor's degree in finance, economics, or another quantitative field, or equivalent practical experience
 Nice to Have 
- Familiarity with project finance structures or energy asset modeling
- Experience in infrastructure, energy, or utility-facing businesses
- Experience building models that support live deal negotiations
 What Will Help You Succeed 
- Analytical rigor: You build models and analyses that hold up under review. You check your work before you share it and you catch inconsistencies in the data underneath.
- Assumption validation: You are comfortable going to other teams for the inputs you need, pressure-testing what you get back, and raising a discrepancy before it lands in a pricing output.

Finance · Remote (US) · Full-time · Reports to Director of Finance

Care plans change how pets receive care. Pet owners pay a predictable monthly amount, visit more often, and catch problems earlier. Hospitals build steadier revenue and longer client relationships. Our mission is to make that kind of preventive care available to every pet.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Our financial models have two audiences. Internally, they guide how we plan, hire, and raise capital. Externally, they help a large veterinary network decide whether to partner with us, and the EBITDA lift model and pricing proposal are often what a network's CFO evaluates before signing. You will spend about 70% of your time on FP&A and about 30% on customer-facing modeling. The work rewards people who ask why a number is what it is, can turn a vague question into a structured analysis, and care whether the reader understands the answer. After a year, you will own the operating model, the board package, and the standard enterprise proposal model, and the sales team will bring you into late-stage deals as a matter of course.




RESPONSIBILITIES

FP&A (about 70%)

 - Maintain and extend the operating model, including the revenue forecast, expenses, cash flow, and runway.

 - Prepare the monthly management report and the board package.

 - Lead model design and variance analysis for the annual budget and reforecasts, working directly with department leads.

 - Track unit economics by segment and by hospital, including acquisition cost, lifetime value, gross margin, and contribution margin.

 - Build investor-ready models, scenario analyses, and data room materials during fundraising.

 - Build and maintain management reporting and self-service dashboards in Sigma.

Customer-facing modeling (about 30%)

 - Maintain the EBITDA lift model and unit economics framework we present to enterprise prospects.

 - Model custom proposals across adoption levels, plan designs, fee structures, and rebates, showing the effect on both the customer's economics and Nest's margins.

 - Model revenue recognition for enterprise customers under ASC 606, including allocation, consumption-based recognition, straight-line amortization, and breakage.

 - Join customer calls when a CFO or procurement team wants to test assumptions on incrementality and ROI.

 - Analyze performance across our live hospitals, including spend lift, visit frequency, cancellations, breakage, and payment capture.
   
   


WHO YOU ARE

We are looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements for this role. If you meet them, we encourage you to apply. Preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.




MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS

 - You have 4 or more years in FP&A, investment banking, consulting, or finance at a SaaS or healthcare company.

 - You build financial models that are clean, auditable, and ready to show a board or a customer.

 - You write your own SQL against a warehouse such as BigQuery or Snowflake.

 - You understand SaaS economics, including ARR, retention, CAC, LTV, and payback, and the accounting underneath them.

 - You have presented analysis to senior audiences and handled hard questions about it.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Working knowledge of ASC 606 and subscription billing.

Compliance teams at banks and fintechs are drowning in financial crimes investigations. The harder problem is underneath. Whether the team is five analysts or 500, they share one brain. Every memory carries provenance. Agents propose; humans approve. That's four years of identity infrastructure sitting under the agent, and it's the part nobody can bolt on later.

- Build, test, and scale new initiatives, then transition them to long-term owners
- Support hiring and org-building as the team scales
- Take on ambiguous, high-priority problems with full ownership

- Strong analytical skills with experience working directly with data, dashboards, and reporting (SQL preferred or willingness to learn)
- Proven ability to own metrics and operating cadence in a fast-paced environment
- Strong prioritization and judgment in ambiguous, high-change environments

- Background in healthcare, marketplace, or operations-heavy environments preferred
- Highly organized, detail-oriented, and proactive in identifying problems before raised
- Motivated by outcomes over ownership and effective in collaborative environments
- MBA a plus, but not required

description:
Profound is the fastest-growing AI marketing platform, used by 15% of the Fortune 500 including Comcast, Estée Lauder, and Walmart, and innovators like Ramp, MongoDB, and Figma. It is where marketing teams do the work: research, briefs, content, campaigns, reporting, all in one place, alongside agents that carry the load with them.  

Built on 2B+ real user prompts and growing, Profound’s data shows you what people ask AI and what the models say back. Profound's AI Marketer joins that data with deep context about our customers to find the opportunities worth acting on, and then puts agents to work: automating reporting, drafting content, auditing pages for readability, running competitive research. It measures what works and gets better every day.

We are hiring for Strategic Finance and Operations as a high-impact, early finance hire to help build the financial backbone of one of the fastest-growing companies in AI. This is a true Swiss army knife role, hands-on, fast-moving, and high-visibility. You will partner with every team at Profound, and no two weeks will look the same.

The ideal candidate holds themselves to a high bar, moves quickly without sacrificing precision, and thrives when given ownership to lead work from start to finish.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Drive strategic analyses that inform how we price, invest, and compete, translating complex data into clear recommendations for the business

 - Partner with Sales, RevOps, Marketing, and Engineering as the connective tissue between Finance and the rest of the company

 - Help build the financial infrastructure for a company expanding internationally

 - Build and maintain financial models that drive planning, investment decisions, and long-term growth

 - Take on high-impact ad hoc projects that do not fit neatly into a job description but provide outsized leverage to the business




WHO YOU ARE

 - 3 to 7 years of experience in strategic finance, FP&A, investment banking, management consulting, or a similarly rigorous analytical role, with high-growth SaaS experience strongly preferred

 - Technically sharp and able to turn ambiguous data into a narrative that drives strategic decision-making

 - Fluent in SaaS business models and able to connect metrics to the operating decisions that move them

 - Excellent written and verbal communicator who can make complex ideas land with any audience

 - High ownership and low ego, caring more about getting it right than getting credit

 - Naturally curious with a bias toward action, eager to dig in, figure it out, and move things forward without waiting to be asked




LOCATION

This is an on-site role based in our NYC or SF office, designed for builders who thrive on speed, iteration, and meaningful impact.

For this role, the expected base salary range is $115,000 to $220,000 (NYC and SF). Profound’s total compensation package is designed to be competitive and includes base salary, equity, and a full range of benefits and perks. Final compensation will depend on factors such as your skills, experience, qualifications, and location, and will be determined during the interview process. Our recruiting team will share more details about the full compensation package and benefits as you move through hiring.

Note: All official communication from Profound will come from a @tryprofound.com email address. If you're contacted by anyone using a different domain, please disregard and report it as spam.

About Us: 
 The people of Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (MSK) are united by a singular mission: ending cancer for life. Our specialized care teams provide personalized, compassionate, expert care to patients of all ages. MSK is dedicated to training the next generation of scientists and clinicians, who go on to pursue our mission at MSK and around the globe. 
 Exciting Opportunity at MSK: Workforce Coordinator    
 At Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (MSK), our people are the foundation of our mission to end cancer for life. This role supports nursing workforce planning through the accurate management of employee records and workforce data, helping to ensure seamless staffing operations and an exceptional experience for nursing employees.  
 This role is ideal for a detail-oriented professional who enjoys balancing operational excellence with service. By maintaining data integrity, coordinating workforce transactions, and supporting workforce planning processes, the coordinator contributes to a highly effective nursing workforce that enables the delivery of world-class patient care.  
 Role Overview   
- Maintain accurate and up-to-date employee records throughout the employment lifecycle.  
- Process workforce transactions, including hires, transfers, status changes, leaves of absence, and separations.  
- Support Nurse Workforce Planning initiatives through timely and accurate staff record maintenance.  
- Review and validate employee documentation to ensure completeness, accuracy, and compliance with established standards.  
- Serve as a resource for employees and leaders regarding staff records and workforce administration processes.  
- Manage electronic personnel files, document retention activities, and records organization.  
- Generate workforce-related reports and provide data support for audits and operational reviews.  
- Partner with Payroll and nursing leadership to ensure accurate workforce information and seamless operations.  
- Identify and support process improvement initiatives that enhance efficiency, accuracy, and service delivery.  
 Key Qualifications   
- 2+ years of experience in workforce administration, staff records, healthcare operations, or a related function.  
- Experience working with HRIS or workforce management systems and employee data.  
- Knowledge of records management, documentation standards, and data integrity practices.  
- Demonstrated ability to manage confidential information with discretion and professionalism.  
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, Word, Outlook, and Teams.  
 Core Skills   
- Exceptional attention to detail and commitment to accuracy.  
- Strong organizational and time-management skills with the ability to prioritize competing demands.  
- Customer-focused approach with a commitment to delivering responsive and high-quality service.  
- Effective verbal and written communication skills with the ability to collaborate across stakeholder groups.  
- Strong problem-solving capabilities and a continuous improvement mindset.

description:
Accountabilities:
- Lead Business Discovery and Stakeholder Collaboration: Conduct interviews, workshops, and process walkthroughs to understand business challenges, objectives, stakeholder expectations, and success criteria. Build strong relationships with Account Management teams, specialty healthcare providers, subject matter experts, and technical delivery teams.
- Analyze Contract Eligibility and Pricing Data: Review contract eligibility and pricing information to identify discrepancies, data gaps, pricing errors, and underlying root causes. Validate contract configurations, customer eligibility, and pricing accuracy against customer records and Group Purchasing Organization (GPO) membership data.

- Demonstrated experience working with healthcare Group Purchasing Organization (GPO) membership data, customer rosters, contract eligibility, and pricing structures.
- Advanced knowledge of healthcare contract pricing, including pricing tiers, effective and expiration dates, invoice pricing, chargebacks, credit transactions, and rebilling processes.
- Strong understanding of healthcare customer identifiers and account hierarchies, including GLN, HIN, DEA, and account numbers, as well as parent-child customer relationships and how they connect customers to contracts.
- Familiarity with healthcare Account Management processes and specialty provider operations, including business decisions, operational controls, workflows, and expected outcomes.
- Experience supporting specialty provider customers within pharmaceutical distribution is highly desirable.
- Proficiency in SQL for data analysis, querying, reconciliation, and validation.
- Experience using SAP, Tableau, and Alteryx to support business analysis, reporting, and data-driven decision-making.
- Ability to translate complex business processes and operational requirements into structured functional, technical, and data specifications.
- Strong analytical and critical-thinking skills, with the ability to investigate discrepancies, identify root causes, and recommend practical solutions.
- Experience facilitating stakeholder interviews, workshops, and cross-functional discussions to gather requirements and resolve conflicting interpretations.
- Understanding of data quality, source-system relationships, business rules, and data governance principles.
- Experience developing acceptance criteria, UAT scenarios, test cases, and validation processes.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical and analytical concepts to both business and technical audiences.
- Strong organizational and documentation skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and maintain requirements traceability throughout project delivery.

description:

 Gibson Dunn is a leading global law firm, advising clients on significant transactions and disputes. Our exceptional teams craft and deploy creative legal strategies that are meticulously tailored to every matter, however complex or high stakes. The firm’s work is distinguished by a unique combination of precision and vision.
 The Research and Information Management (RIM) Department provides research assistance to the Firm’s attorneys and business services departments. The RIM Department oversees all research and online subscriptions operating in a fast-paced environment.  The candidate must be flexible and highly committed to quality, customer service, teamwork and supporting Firm and department.
 Based in NY or DC, the Senior Research Analyst- Litigation will be responsible for providing comprehensive research services to attorneys within the firm. This role involves conducting in-depth legal and business research across all the firm’s practice areas and supporting the firm's AI initiatives. The position requires a strong understanding of research databases as well as excellent communication and analytical skills. The candidate should possess a keen interest in innovation and technology, and an ability to learn new legal and business research platforms. 
 The role reports to the DC Research Manager.
 Responsibilities include: 
- Conduct in-depth legal research across all practice groups, including complex, litigation and multijurisdictional requests requiring advanced research strategy and analytical judgment.
- Independently manage research assignments, preparing comprehensive analysis of results and delivery in a timely manner.
- Contributes to training curriculum development and delivery for RIM Analysts, and assisting with onboarding, orientation and training for attorneys and staff on research resources.
- Utilize GenAI tools and emerging technologies to enhance research quality, streamlining workflows and delivering analytical results.
- Conduct client development research support, including background checks and competitive intelligence on current or potential clients and markets.
- Evaluate new resources, including conducting resource trials, assessments and making recommendations to RIM leadership.
- Remain current on research techniques and available resources relevant to providing high-quality research and information services.
- Participate in rotating weekend coverage.
 Qualifications: 
- Ability to define problems, collect data, establish facts, and draw valid conclusions.
- Demonstrated ability to exercise independent judgment and discretion on research matters of significance, applying advanced and specialized knowledge with minimal supervision.
- Excellent oral and written communication skills.
- Strong level of attention to detail and accuracy.
- Service-oriented team player with the ability to interact with individuals at all levels of the organization and provide platinum client service.
- Ability to work in a fast-paced environment with demonstrated ability to coordinate multiple projects and initiatives simultaneously while meeting deadlines and business objectives.
- Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a hybrid team environment.
- Ability to solve problems and work well under pressure despite strict deadlines.
 Experience: 
- Master’s in library science (MLS) or equivalent, or JD preferred.
- A minimum of six to eight years of related experience providing research services in a law firm or professional services organization.
- Thorough knowledge of professional library science and research techniques using various resources required.
- Experience supporting litigation practice groups.
- Experience utilizing Quest as a centralized ticketing system for incoming research requests a plus.
- Proficient in the use of various legal research databases such as Lexis+, Westlaw Precision, CoCounsel, Bloomberg Law, Lex Machina, Trellis, Newsdesk, and other related resources.

Are you passionate about turning data into insights that drive business impact? 
 Do you thrive at the intersection of analytics, technology, procurement, and AI, helping teams make better decisions through trusted data?

 Our team implements and administers policy and/or administration of short or long-term international assignments. We oversee immigration services, policies, and regulations to ensure compliance. We execute functional business plans and contribute to the development of functional global mobility strategy, guiding decisions by divisional strategy. 
 About the Role 
 Reporting to the Head of GP Finance and Analytics, you will play a key role in advancing RELX Global Procurement's data and analytics capabilities. You will own reporting for critical supplier data, help scale a modern operational data layer using Microsoft Dataverse and Power Apps, and partner with procurement professionals to deliver insights, reporting, and AI-enabled solutions that support sourcing and strategic initiatives. This role offers the opportunity to influence data governance, improve decision-making, and drive operational excellence across a global procurement organization. 
 Responsibilities 
- Own consolidated reporting for GP-owned operational data tracked at the parent-supplier level, including price protection, contacts, code of conduct, ESG/Carbon metrics, and critical supplier dimensions 
- Serve as a subject matter expert for Microsoft Dataverse and Power Apps, advising on new use cases and capabilities 
- Partner closely with the GP Technology team, providing analytic, AI, and general support across sourcing and strategic initiatives 
- Identify, investigate, and resolve spend data anomalies in collaboration with the GP Data Analytics Senior Manager 
- Lead periodic reporting on Global Procurement key performance objectives against targets 
- Maintain users and suppliers for Dun & Bradstreet key supplier alerts to support early risk detection 
- Establish and maintain data governance standards, including ownership, access controls, quality checks, and audit trails 
- Contribute analytics, reporting, and strategic communications that help drive procurement outcomes 
 Requirements 
- Background in financial or operational reporting and analytics 
- AI fluency, practical LLM capabilities, and commitment to continuous development and use of AI skills 
- Experience with Microsoft Dataverse and Power Apps 
- Strong Excel skills; Alteryx experience is a plus 
- Comfort working with large datasets and data enrichment concepts, including parentage and classification 
- Ability to break down complex problems, identify root causes, and develop practical solutions 
- Strong written and oral communication skills with close attention to detail 
- Ability to collaborate effectively across finance, technology, and procurement teams 
 Work in a Way That Works for You 
 We promote a healthy work/life balance across the organisation. We offer an appealing working prospect for our people. With numerous wellbeing initiatives, shared parental leave, study assistance, and sabbaticals, we will help you meet your immediate responsibilities and your long-term goals. 
 Working Pattern 
 Working flexible hours - flexing the times when you work in the day to help you fit everything in and work when you are the most productive.

The company has four market segments. It develops information-based analytics and decision tools for professional and business customers in the Risk, Scientific, Technical & Medical, Legal, and Exhibitions sectors.
