About the Position 
 The Interstate Renewable Energy Council (IREC) is seeking an organized, people-focused program associate to join its Workforce team. Working with the Vice President, Workforce Strategy & Innovation, workforce colleagues, and partners, you will help job seekers find their way into clean energy careers and help move projects from workplan to delivery. 
 A core part of this role is serving as the first point of contact for all Workforce inquiries. You will help job seekers explore clean energy careers, understand training and Registered Apprenticeship options, and connect with training providers, employers, and workforce programs. You will also triage technical assistance requests from training providers, employers, and other partners, answering what you can and routing the rest to the right staff lead. In addition, you will coordinate group technical assistance, office hours, and webinars; keep information on Green Workforce Connect, IREC's workforce platform, current and accurate; and maintain the records the team relies on to meet its commitments. 
 The role also contributes to outreach, writing, and resource development. You will help recruit employers, training providers, and job seekers into IREC's programs; draft communications for partners and job seekers; and research and write practical resources such as fact sheets, guides, and career exploration content. 
 The associate works across IREC's Workforce portfolio as priorities shift, rather than on a single program. This role suits someone with experience supporting job seekers or coordinating programs who writes clearly, manages details well, and builds trust quickly. 
 Responsibilities 
- Serve as the first point of contact for all Workforce inquiries, including job seeker questions and technical assistance requests from training providers, employers, apprenticeship programs, workforce organizations, and other partners. Triage each request, respond directly where you can, route complex requests to the right staff lead, and track each one through to resolution. 
- Help build and maintain the team's intake and referral process, including response standards, a referral map, and follow-up tracking. 
- Learn about job seekers' interests, skills, and goals; explain clean energy/energy efficiency career pathways, training, certification, and Registered Apprenticeship options; and connect people with training providers, apprenticeship programs, employers, and other local resources. 
- Lead or support guided career exploration sessions and one-on-one and small-group follow-up for job seekers, including participants in IREC's online career exploration courses. 
- Support outreach and recruitment that brings employers, training providers, apprenticeship programs, and job seekers into IREC's workforce programs and Green Workforce Connect, communicating program benefits clearly to each audience. 
- Build and maintain relationships with employers, training providers, apprenticeship programs, workforce agencies, and community-based organizations, including outreach to communities underrepresented in clean energy careers. 
- Draft program communications for employers, training providers, workforce partners, and job seekers, including email campaigns, blog posts, event announcements, and other outreach materials. 
- Research, write, and update practical resources, such as fact sheets, guides, career exploration content, and tools that help counselors, navigators, and workforce professionals support job seekers. 
- Help design and deliver presentations and webinar content for partners, workforce professionals, and job seekers. 
- Coordinate group technical assistance sessions, office hours, webinars, workshops, and partner meetings. Confirm audiences and topics with project leads, manage invitations and registration, prepare agendas and materials, coordinate speakers and logistics, and provide meeting support. 
- Support session facilitation by welcoming participants, monitoring questions, documenting themes and action items, collecting feedback, and coordinating referrals and follow-up. 
- Research, vet, and update training-provider, employer, and apprenticeship listings and state and regional resource pages on Green Workforce Connect. 
- Maintain accurate records of inquiries, technical assistance requests, referrals, partner engagement, participation, and outcomes, and prepare summaries and inputs for grant reports.

ABOUT THE COMPANY

Pilots don't train with real passengers. Actors don't rehearse with real audiences. Yet, the most consequential decisions in society are often pushed straight to production.

 

Simile is changing that. We have built the first AI simulation of society, populated by generative agents based on real humans. Our research pioneered the field of AI-based simulation, proving it is possible to model human behavior with high accuracy. Today, we are developing a Foundation Model to predict human behavior in any situation, at any scale.

 

We have raised $300M in total funding, with a $2B post-money valuation in our latest round. Our investors include Greenoaks, Index Ventures, Hanabi, A*, Bain Capital Ventures, Factory, CVS Health Ventures, and Definition.

 


ABOUT THE ROLE

Deployment Strategist at Simile means making sure simulation is deeply valuable to our customers. You’ll get to know their business well enough to see where simulation can change a decision, then help them turn those problems into simulations. You'll take what you learn back to our product and research teams to collaborate on what we build next.

 

The people who do well here are energized by customers and their experience in the product: building relationships, digging into hard problems, and staying on top of the details. You'll move fast, have real ownership early, and work closely with product and research on problems that matter to Fortune 500 organizations across industries.

 

We work with customers across a wide range of industries, including healthcare, pharma, retail, CPG, financial services and entertainment. Depending on your past experience, your interests and the team’s needs, you may work with one customer or several, in one vertical or across a few. We’ll talk through this with you during your interviews.

 


IDEALLY, YOU'D HAVE:

Experience from one of three areas:

 1. Operators coming from companies that deploy enterprise AI or data products

 2. Strategy consultants or investors who want to move into tech to own outcomes

 3. PMs or engineers who got pulled into the business and customer side and never looked back

 


IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Own your Customers: Be the person your customers rely on - responsive, on top of the details, and trusted to get things done

 - Drive Deployments: Own enterprise customer engagements from first call to full deployment and beyond

 - Know the Product: Go deep on Simile's platform - simulations, population modeling, evals, and validations - and bring that knowledge into every customer conversation

 - Work Cross-functionally: Bridge the gap between what customers need and what product and modeling teams build, and make sure the right insights from the field shape internal decisions

 - Shape the Business: Take on high-impact projects that span the full business - from how we land new customers to how we think about simulation quality and what we build next

 


REQUIREMENTS


MUST HAVES

 - Mindset: Thrives in ambiguous, 0-1 environments - scrappy, resourceful, and doesn't wait to be told what to do

 - Reliability: The person your teammates and customers can count on - detail-oriented, accountable, and consistent

 - Customer Focus: Exceptional communicator who builds trust quickly with senior stakeholders and knows how to navigate complex relationships

 - Product Fluency: Able to get up to speed on technical concepts quickly and explain them clearly; no coding required, but comfortable engaging with AI concepts like evals, validation, and model behavior

 - Travel: Willing to travel for customer engagements

 


NICE TO HAVES

 - Comfort building lightweight tools or automations (scripts, no-code tools, etc.)

 - Familiarity with enterprise software deployments or B2B SaaS

 


COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

At Simile, we provide competitive compensation packages that include base salary, equity, and comprehensive benefits.

 - Salary Range: $150,000 – $300,000 USD
   
   - Note: Final offers are based on experience, specialized skills, interview performance, and relevant training.

 - Equity: Grants are available for eligible roles, subject to board approval.

 - Health & Wellness: Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage.

 - Time Off: Flexible time off policies to support work-life balance.

 


OUR PROCESS

We prioritize thoughtful conversations and clear examples of past work. Our hiring journey is designed to help both sides align on fit, working style, and expectations.

 

Reapplication Policy: To ensure a fair and thorough evaluation for all applicants, Simile observes a 90-day waiting period before reconsidering candidates for the same role.

 


COMMITMENT TO DIVERSITY & INCLUSION

Equal Opportunity: Simile is an equal opportunity workplace. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and identities, valuing an environment where everyone can contribute authentically.

 

Accommodations: If you require support or reasonable accommodations during the application process due to a disability, please let us know. We are happy to assist.

About us:

Jerry.ai http://Jerry.ai is a Series C, YC-backed tech startup with 5M+ customers and $240M in funding. Founded in 2017, product launched in 2019, and achieved profitability in 2024.

 

Why we exist:

Your car, home, and motorcycle aren't just purchases, they're the physical embodiment of the life you've worked hard to build. Yet the experience of owning them is stuck in the 90s. Every step of the journey — buying, insuring, maintaining, repairing, selling — is fragmented, complicated, and expensive.

 

Imagine having a trusted friend in your pocket who takes care of everything: they find you the right car or home at the right price, lock in the best insurance rate without you lifting a finger, remind you before that service appointment turns into an expensive repair, and help you sell at the best price when the time is right. That friend is Jerry.

 

We are building the first AI-powered advisor to manage all your physical assets. We started with your car in 2019, now we’re expanding into new verticals (e.g. home, motorcycle, RV, boat).

 

Why We’re Hiring

Our Business Operations & Analytics  team has been a force multiplier and accelerant to our business that has helped us reach these pivotal milestones in spite of headwinds and within a highly competitive market. They are a team of former McKinsey, BCG and Bain consultants who drive data & insights, and inform decision-making across every corner of our business. They are analytical powerhouses and first principles problem solvers who push forward our most important initiatives across product, growth, tech, and operations.

 

Every business unit has a Business Operations & Analytics team member embedded within it  —  someone who doesn't just run analyses and build dashboards, but shapes what questions we should ask, what data to pull, what conclusions to draw, what decisions to make, and then drives our teams towards our next goal: go from 5M to 50M customers and become a $10B business in the next 4 years. 

 

As our business continues to expand, there is growing demand for more Business Operations & Analytics team members. We are hiring 2-3 people to drive impact in these areas:

 - Growth Marketing 

 - Product Development

 - Strategic Partnerships 

 

On leveling: You may see job ads for this role at different job levels. Our priority is finding the right people, we can be flexible with job title/leveling.

 - No slides: If you've worked in consulting, you know what it feels like to be up at 3am reformatting a deck. That doesn't exist here. The only work that gets done at Jerry is work that will materially change the trajectory of our business — an important product, a new growth channel, a key metric, a critical partner relationship, etc. 

 - No corporate fluff: The Business Operations & Analytics team is 14 insatiable learners who care deeply about solving difficult problems and making a tangible impact. Every person owns a critical domain. There is no bloat, unnecessary meetings, or waiting for approvals. 

 - Hands-on: This is not a pure strategy role, you will also own execution. Your day-to-day will be surfacing analytical insights, driving decisions, and seeing them through end-to-end. 

 

What You'll Own

You'll sit on our central Business Operations & Analytics team but you’ll be embedded in one of Jerry's core business areas — growth, product, AI and automation, strategic partnerships — and own the analytical function for that business unit end-to-end.

 - Define the right problems: Before any analysis, understand what business question it's answering and what decision it will inform. Push back if the question is flawed.

 - Data and insights: Define metrics, build reports, run analyses, design experiments, and surface data insights that move your team's key metrics.

 - Drive outcomes: Bring recommendations to your counterparts in product, growth, finance or operations, tell them what's happening and why, and what next steps should be.
Who You Are
 - First principles thinker: You break ambiguous problems into clear hypotheses before touching data. You're analytically strong (comfortable with SQL or Python) but your instinct is to ask "what are we trying to solve here?" before jumping to "what should I build?" 
 - Direct communicator: You can walk a skeptical stakeholder through a complex finding and get buy-in quickly. You write clearly, speak precisely, and don't bury the lede.
 - Owner: You act like your name is on the door. If something is broken, you feel responsible for fixing it, even if it’s outside of your swim lane.
What You'll Bring
 - 2+ years of experience at a consulting firm, investment bank, or high-growth technology company.
 - Strong analytical skills; ability to pull, structure, and interpret data independently.
 - Track record of owning ambiguous problems and delivering impact.
 - Clear, persuasive communicator who can influence decisions at the leadership level.

title: Financial Counselor
description:
Job Summary: The Financial Counselor is a patient-facing member of the central Revenue Cycle Management (RCM) team, responsible for educating infusion patients on their insurance coverage and benefits, conducting patient welcome calls, providing cost estimates, assessing financial need, enrolling patients in co-pay assistance and grant programs, and arranging patient payment plans before treatment begins. The role partners closely with the Infusion Coordinators, who serve as the local point of contact at each clinic site, and with the Benefits Verification/Prior Authorization (BVPA) team to ensure patients are financially cleared, informed, and ready for treatment so infusion orders are processed accurately and on time.

Key Responsibilities:

Patient Financial Counseling & Education (Patient-Facing)

 - Serve as the primary financial contact for patients, communicating with them directly regarding the insurance and financial aspects of their infusion treatment.

 - Conduct patient welcome calls to introduce the financial counseling role, set expectations for the financial clearance process, and answer initial questions about coverage and costs.

 - Obtain and confirm insurance coverage information and demographics prior to the start of treatment.

 - Educate patients on their insurance coverage and verified benefits, including co-pays, deductibles, and out-of-pocket expenses, using benefit information provided by the BVPA team.

 - Assess patients' ability to meet their financial obligations and identify those who may need financial assistance.

 - Prepare and review cost estimates with patients, outlining their expected financial responsibility for infusion treatment based on verified benefits.

 - Discuss payment options and set up payment arrangements with patients and ensure patient responsibility amounts are accurately recorded in the system prior to treatment.

 - Answer patient questions about coverage, authorization status, and costs in a clear, compassionate manner.

Insurance Eligibility & Authorization Requirements

 - Verify insurance eligibility and verify and update demographics and insurance coverage in the system according to established procedures.

 - Track patients' progress through the financial clearance process.

Patient Financial Assistance

 - Screen patients for financial assistance eligibility and refer or enroll those who express financial necessity in manufacturer copay assistance programs and/or foundation grants.

 - Enroll eligible patients in manufacturer co-pay assistance programs, including completing enrollment, confirming activation, and monitoring program benefits and renewals.

 - Complete grant and assistance applications on behalf of patients, gather required documentation in coordination with local teams, and follow up on application decisions and renewals.

 - Stay current on available financial assistance programs and build professional relationships with manufacturer programs and foundations to identify additional resources for patients.

 - Track enrollment and grant status and communicate confirmation of financial assistance enrollment to Infusion Coordinators so patients can be scheduled.

Communication, Collaboration & Documentation

 - Communicate with patients and providers regarding the insurance and financial status of infusion orders.

 - Work collaboratively with Infusion Coordinators, the BVPA team, and other central RCM colleagues to resolve financial barriers and keep orders moving.

 - Document all patient, payer, and provider communications and financial activity in designated systems (e.g., Athena, WeInfuse) and maintain accurate logs and records.

 - Adhere to HIPAA and all applicable confidentiality, state, and federal requirements regarding patient information.

Qualifications:

 - High school diploma or equivalent; associate degree in finance or business, or equivalent revenue cycle experience, preferred

 - Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including superior interpersonal and patient contact skills, excellent telephone manners, and the ability to explain insurance terminology clearly to patients

 - Minimum of two years of patient benefits experience preferred, with experience in financial counseling, pre-service coordination, or insurance billing for medical services and general knowledge of ICD-10 and CPT codes; infusion or specialty medication experience is a plus

 - Working knowledge of insurance coverage, benefits, and terminology (co-pays, deductibles, out-of-pocket maximums), and experience preparing patient cost estimates and arranging payment plans

 - Experience with financial assistance, copay assistance, or grant applications is a plus

 - Experience with, or ability to quickly learn, EHR and infusion management systems (e.g., Athena, WeInfuse)

 - Knowledge of medical terminology and clinical documentation review

 - Compassion and professionalism when discussing sensitive financial topics with patients

 - Strong organizational skills

 - Detail-oriented

 - Ability to multi-task and work well in a fast-paced setting

 - Critical thinking skills and decisive judgment

Work Environment & Location:

This position may be based in person at a clinic site or remote, and includes direct communication with patients by phone, virtually, and/or in person.

Blossom Health exists to solve the mental health epidemic in America by partnering with psychiatrists to expand access to affordable, timely, clinically effective mental healthcare. Our AI-native care platform is loved by hundreds of clinicians and thousands of patients.

We're a Series A company with $20M+ raised from Headline, Village Global, and the founders of General Catalyst, Flatiron Health, Sword Health, Grow Therapy, Fay, Elemy, Zip, Blank Street, Assured, Bridge, Birches Health, and Enzo Health.

We're growing quickly and building the technology, systems, and infrastructure to transform how mental healthcare is delivered.


THE ROLE

We're hiring a Product & Business Operations Lead to own some of the most important and complex challenges behind scaling Blossom Health.

This isn't a traditional operations role. You'll work at the intersection of product, technology, business operations, and strategic partnerships, turning complex, manual processes into intelligent, scalable systems.

One day, you might be redesigning how we credential hundreds of clinicians across multiple states. The next, you could be partnering with engineering to automate a critical workflow, negotiating with a payer, or building the infrastructure that unlocks an entirely new market.

We're not looking for someone who simply manages processes. We want someone who questions why they exist, figures out how to make them 10x better, and builds systems that scale.

You'll report directly to our Founder, work closely with leaders across the company, and have the autonomy to take ambitious ideas from problem identification through execution.


WHY YOU SHOULD WORK HERE

 - 🚀 Be early in a hyper-growth startup: Join the foundational team of a rapidly scaling Series A company and help build the infrastructure behind our next stage of growth.

 - 📈 Build things that actually move the business: Your work won't live in a presentation. You'll own initiatives that directly impact how we operate, expand, and deliver care to patients.

 - 🤝 High trust and autonomy: Work directly with our Founder and take ownership of meaningful problems from day one, with the freedom to shape how they're solved.

 - 🧠 Work at the intersection of AI, product, and operations: Rethink how traditional healthcare processes work by leveraging technology, automation, and AI to build smarter systems.

 - 🏃 We move with speed and purpose: Join a talent-dense team that values intellectual curiosity, high standards, and people who turn ambitious ideas into reality.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

Build the infrastructure behind our growth

 - Own critical operational functions end-to-end, including provider credentialing, payer workflows, and revenue cycle operations.

 - Design and implement scalable systems that support our expansion across providers, payers, and markets.

 - Identify operational bottlenecks, uncover root causes, and build lasting solutions rather than temporary fixes.

 - Develop monitoring systems, performance metrics, and automated workflows that make operations more reliable and efficient.

Turn operational challenges into product and technology solutions

 - Partner directly with engineering to build internal tools, automation, and AI-powered workflows.

 - Translate complex business problems into clear product requirements and technical solutions.

 - Identify opportunities to replace manual processes with technology, AI agents, and intelligent systems.

 - Think beyond individual problems to design infrastructure that prevents them from recurring.

Drive strategic partnerships and business development

 - Negotiate with external stakeholders and drive initiatives from initial conversations through implementation.

 [...]  - You have 2–6 years of professional experience in business operations, product operations, strategy, consulting, or a high-growth technology startup.

To achieve these goals, we’re building both a new technological foundation that draws inspiration from how humans reason, and a new kind of collaborative organization that puts human values first.

description:
ABOUT US

Kingdom is the world’s first AI-native ingredients company.  We create Superculture® ingredients from natural microbes to improve the health of pets and people. Brands use our ingredients because they deliver industry-leading efficacy and health benefits that consumers notice in just days.

AI powers how we develop, clinically validate, and manufacture our ingredients, enabling us to bring them to market faster and at lower cost.  Developing a new ingredient has traditionally taken more than five years and tens of millions of dollars.  Our small team is launching one clinically validated ingredient a year, at a small fraction of that cost.

Kingdom has clear product-market fit, with accelerating customer demand:

 - After just a year in market, our ingredients are already in dozens of products from household pet brands. And 95% of our first-time customers are launching additional products with us.

 - Each ingredient improves our discovery platform, clinical engine, and manufacturing expertise, so we can develop the next one faster and at lower cost.

 - We’ve raised nearly $40M from leading investors to bring our ingredients to more brands and markets around the world.

Our number one priority is turning proven ingredient performance and early commercial traction into repeatable growth across customers and markets. We’re looking for highly resourceful, high-throughput individuals who solve problems from first principles, make sound decisions, communicate clearly, and move quickly.

More than $300B is spent every year on pet and human health products.  Our ambition is to make clinical efficacy the standard across that entire market.

All full-time roles are in person at our Brooklyn Navy Yard headquarters and lab.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Kingdom is at an inflection point. Demand for our Superculture® pet ingredients is accelerating, and we are preparing to commercialize our first human ingredient. Every one of those ingredients starts in the same place: our biobank. Growing and maintaining that collection of microbes, and generating the sequencing data that tells us what we have, is foundational to everything we build.

The Research Associate II, Microbiology is at the center of that work. You will join our lab team to own day-to-day biobanking and sequencing operations, from processing new sources and isolating novel strains, to keeping our existing collection healthy, to running PCR, library prep, and sequencing.

If you’re an early-career scientist looking to deepen your experience in microbiology and molecular biology, take ownership of a range of workstreams, and grow with a fast-moving biotech, we want to hear from you.




IF YOU JOIN, YOU WILL:

 - Grow and maintain Kingdom’s biobank by obtaining, processing, and organizing sources, isolating new strains, regenerating older strains, and making and cataloging strain stocks

 - Culture and isolate microbes using rigorous aseptic technique, working with BSL-1 and BSL-2 strains and with anaerobes in our anaerobic chambers

 - Obtain pure isolates and prepare screening plates to support new projects

 - Run PCR and gel purification for Sanger sequencing needs

 - Own DNA extraction and library preparation for 16S/ITS and whole genome sequencing

 - Run qPCR assays and process the resulting data

 - Use liquid handlers to scale high-throughput methods, and troubleshoot and improve protocols along the way

 - Execute on in vitro cell-based models

 - Support experimental characterization of Superculture® ingredients




WE’RE LOOKING FOR YOU IF YOU HAVE:

 - A BS or MS in microbiology, molecular biology, or a related life-sciences field

 - 1–2 years of hands-on experience in a microbiology or molecular biology lab, in academia or industry

 - Strong aseptic technique and direct experience isolating and culturing microbes, including preparing culture media

 - Hands-on experience with DNA extraction, PCR, gel electrophoresis, and sequencing library preparation

 - Meticulous execution and documentation habits, with bench work that others can trace and reproduce
 - Experience with lab automation, including liquid handlers
 - Strong organization, with the ability to juggle requests from multiple teams and meet turnaround commitments
 - A troubleshooting mindset and the drive to find and fix problems without waiting to be asked
WORKING WITH US
Kingdom is based in the Brooklyn Navy Yard, with our full team working out of a 9,000 sq-ft headquarters and lab space.  We operate in a high-trust, high-autonomy environment, which requires that everyone uphold our core values:
 - Solve from first principles. We have a deep-seated curiosity about the most important problems facing the business. Our nature is to dig deeply into their details, question assumptions, understand the smallest details, and drive towards the best possible solution using these insights. This makes us very effective in crafting new solutions and operating in ambiguous circumstances.
 - Collaborate with kindness. We are very low ego, and treat each other with respect, compassion, and humility. We hold one another to high standards, but do so while being deeply committed to each other's wellbeing. We invest in each other's growth, and are willing to engage in difficult conversations and deliver direct, constructive feedback when necessary.
 - Be resourceful and resilient. We figure out how to make things work, and how to accomplish our goals regardless of what stands in the way. We're keen to confront challenges together through proactive planning and scrappy methods. When things go wrong, we learn quickly from our missteps, adapt our approach, and push forward.

title: Policy Lab Contributors - Biodiversity Finance
description:
Policy Lab is joint initiative between Journal of Applied Ecology and the BES Policy Team. We aim to synthesize existing research to facilitate policy change by convening the academic community around policy questions that are impactful and time-sensitive, yet may not have been recently or explicitly addressed by the ecological community.
 Policy Lab has two outputs: a Policy Direction article in Journal of Applied Ecology which synthesizes existing research to contribute to policy questions, and a BES Policy Brief which applies the synthesis within a specific context.
 Join the 2027 Policy Lab
 This year we are holding an open call for contributors to explore the question:
 'How should we measure biodiversity outcomes for nature finance?'
 Application deadline : Friday 20 November 2026, 23:59 BST
 In-person workshop : Thursday 21 January 2027 at the BES offices in London
 Online workshops : February 2027 - April 2027
 What are we looking for?
 We are looking to put together a global team of experts who can help us to:
- Answer the question 'How should we measure biodiversity outcomes for nature finance?'
- Write a Policy Direction paper to be submitted to Journal of Applied Ecology to inform and influence policy discussions and future research
- Work with the BES to develop a Policy Brief , getting the answer directly into the hands of policymakers when they need it
 Project timeline 
 We will assess all applications after the closing date and will be in touch to inform you whether your application was successful. If you are selected to join the Policy Lab team, you will be expected to attend an online meeting to meet the rest of the team and learn more about the project.
 Following that, we will meet in person before the British Ecological Society’s (BES) offices in London for the in person workshop. The workshop forms the most important work of the Policy Lab so it is essential to have attendance. We encourage as many people to attend in person as possible, but we will run the workshop hybrid to allow for global representation.
 From January 2027 onwards, we will meet regularly online to work towards completing the Policy Direction and Policy Brief by April 30, 2027. After publication, we will utilise the British Ecological Society’s network and resources to promote the Policy Brief and the paper.[/bliss-accordion]
 How should we measure biodiversity outcomes for nature finance?
 Nature finance is growing quickly, from biodiversity credits , net gain units and nature-enhanced carbon credits to outcome-based bonds and portfolio-level disclosure. Each depends on claims about biodiversity or nature outcomes, yet the ecological community has no agreed view on how those outcomes should be measured. Biodiversity is multidimensional in both its constitution and its value, and no single metric can capture it. The same goes for nature. Financial institutions increasingly recognise this and are looking to ecologists for guidance on which metrics and weights to use, and when.
 This Policy Lab will bring together ecologists from diverse backgrounds to assess the state of measurement for nature finance. The workshop will focus on what needs to be measured, how requirements differ with the purpose of each financial instrument, and whether the community can agree on a coherent set of metrics with clear rules for weighting them to context. It will also consider how measurement should be coordinated across sites, who certifies the metrics and prevents gaming, and how measures can stay back-compatible as monitoring and understanding improve.
 The resulting Policy Direction paper and BES Policy Brief will set out ecologically grounded recommendations for policymakers, standard setters and the finance sector.
 Requirements 
 You must be willing to:
- Be an author on a Policy Direction paper, and contribute to the Policy Brief
- Attend an workshop in London in January 2027 - international contributors are encouraged to attend online
- Attend maximum of one online meeting per month from January to April 2027
 Benefits 
- Join a global team of ecologists working to make real-world impact
- The chance to impact real-world policy and make a difference with your research
- Paper submitted to the esteemed Journal of Applied Ecology

title: Sr. Research Associate
description:
About Us

We are a private design studio that builds and supports a portfolio of companies and projects across software, hardware, hospitality, and more. Some of what we build stays in house; some spins out. We also run an early-stage investment fund and an accompanying cohort program for founders. This company is not Expa, but is an affiliate of Expa's.

The Role

We're looking for a Senior Research Associate who can find out anything about anything. Leadership will come to you with questions — size this market, map the players in this category, who's funding what, what the landscape looks like for XYZ — and you'll come back with an answer that's clear, well-sourced, and actually useful.

Some weeks that means building a competitive matrix across 40 companies. Some weeks it means a deep dive into a single obscure question nobody has written about yet. The projects change, the subject matter changes, and the volume varies week to week.

You'll be exposed to a lot of different projects and ideas, and work directly with a highly accomplished leader and team. If you're the kind of person who reads everything, asks a lot of questions, and wants to be in the room with people operating at a very high level, this is built for you.

What You'll Do

 - Run open-ended research projects using the internet as your primary tool: markets, products, companies, funding activity, competitive landscapes, people, technologies, regulation — whatever the question requires.

 - Turn messy findings into clean outputs: matrices, comparison tables, briefs, landscape maps, one-pagers.

 - Go deep enough to have a point of view, not just a link dump — flag what matters, what's uncertain, and what you'd look at next.

 - Use AI tools aggressively to move faster and go wider than a person could alone.

 - Build lightweight tools, scrapers, or trackers when a project calls for it.

 - Juggle several unrelated requests at once and reprioritize when things shift.

What We're Looking For

 - 2–5 years of experience and a bachelor's degree — you take a task and run with it, but you've got the reps to produce senior-level output: quick turnaround, sharp judgment calls, and less hand-holding needed along the way.

 - Brain power: sharp, curious, and able to reason through a question you've never seen before.

 - AI-native: You live in AI tools — Claude and Cowork, ChatGPT, Gemini, Hugging Face, whatever's newest. Ideally you can vibe code your way to a working script or prototype without waiting on an engineer. Bonus points if you've hit your usage limit more than once.

 - Comfortable in ambiguity: Vague briefs don't paralyze you. You take a first pass, come back with questions, and iterate.

 - Self-directed but coachable: You think independently, but you want to learn from people far ahead of you and take direction well.

 - Startup-minded: You're not looking for a corporate ladder. You want interesting problems, smart people, and range.

 - A strong writer: Your research is only as good as your ability to communicate it in a page or less.

Compensation & Benefits

 - Salary: The anticipated base salary range for this position is $100,000-$130,000. Actual compensation will be determined based on factors including experience, qualifications, level, and location.

 - Benefits: Generous benefits package including medical, dental, and vision, 401(k) matching

 - Location: Can be remote in the US, with significant travel to Los Angeles

title: Financial Scriptwriter
description:
About Future Finance
 A capital-intelligence media brand - newsletter, LinkedIn, X and YouTube. Future Finance doesn't sell directly; it builds reach and credibility, then hands qualified demand to the rest of the group.
 The audience is US-based, 45-plus, net worth above $1M. They understand macro but don't know how to act on it - intelligent, busy, and sold to constantly.
 The brand register is calm, premium and institutional. It never slides into wealth-guru, outrage or doom media, because the audience we want won't trust that tone. This matters more than anything else in this hire.
 The role
 You write Future Finance's long-form YouTube scripts - 30 to 35 minutes, roughly 4,200 words, one per week - and own the research behind every claim in them, so every claim traces to a primary document. You also cut 3–4 short-form scripts from each episode for distribution.
 You do not pick topics and you do not own packaging (titles, thumbnails). That stays with the showrunner and the production agency. You do not name the channel's proprietary frameworks - those come from Salim. You may write about a mechanism he's already explained; you won't invent one and hand it to him to defend on camera.
 What success looks like
- One publish-ready script a week, minimum - four a month, delivered as a full package: research memo, six-beat hook, body, retention map, SHOW/SOURCE tags inline, self-scored review sheet.
- Clears the review gate at 7 of 9 or better on first submission, scored against the Future Finance Content Standard.
- Zero unsourced factual claims - every claim carries a SOURCE tag to a primary document, both sides of contested arguments get argued, and thin research gets flagged, never filled in with a plausible number.
- Retention targets on the finished episode - 70%+ first-minute retention, average view duration above the channel baseline.
- Compliance held on every script - no predictions, no recommendations, no certainty language about what happens next.

title: Research Associate - Data Curation
description:
Are you fascinated by the way science impacts society and do you love diving deep into the scientific literature? Do you enjoy curating data and extracting insights to help advance science? If you are a curious and rigorous data enthusiast, and want to help drug discovery scientists be more effective in creating new medicines, we want to hear from you! 
 Drug Hunter™ ( drughunter.com ) is an essential scientific intelligence platform for R&D innovators turning molecules into medicines. The Drug Hunter team distills the research behind emerging drugs and technologies into concise, but scientifically rich, searchable articles and interactive features. Drug Hunter customers include many of the world’s leading innovative biotechnology and pharmaceutical companies, as well as top-tier investors.
 We are seeking a rigorous data curator to join the Drug Hunter team to cover emerging drug discovery patents and other disclosures. For example, you will be responsible for triaging and curating data from scientific papers and patents, including interpreting chemical structures and biological data to surface the most important insights for our readers. The successful candidate will exhibit a high level of drug discovery scientific knowledge, with strong attention to detail and a keen focus on accuracy . An ability to interpret chemical structures and biological data is a must, as is experience reading the primary scientific and patent literature. 
 This role reports to a Scientific Director and is a full time , fully remote position for candidates based in North America.
 Key Responsibilities 
- Conduct in-depth research, curation, and interpretation of scientific data from the drug discovery-related scientific and patent literature
- Maintain high levels of rigor and accuracy in data curation and analysis, as well as the construction of databases
- Interpretation of chemical structures and biological data 
- Contribute to data research and curation across a range of projects 
- Maintain familiarity with the biopharmaceutical industry, including an understanding of the R&D process from target discovery to commercialization, and key players in the drug discovery and development ecosystem 
- Contribute to a positive culture within the Scientific and Data teams aligned with the mission and values of the company; prioritizing facts, community, clarity, helpfulness, teamwork, and accountability
 Additional Duties 
- Perform other related tasks as necessary to support the ongoing needs of Drug Hunter’s Scientific and Data teams, and associated functions
 Requirements 
 Qualifications 
- Authorization to work in the employee’s location. Drug Hunter cannot provide US visa/Green Card sponsorship or related support relevant to the employee’s location.
- Strong track record of data curation, with an understanding of the patent processes and patent databases
- Ability to interpret chemical structures and biological data, as well as a familiarity with ChemDraw or similar chemical drawing software
- Experience using spreadsheets, such as Excel, Google Sheets, or LibreOffice Calc
- Familiarity with scientific databases and chemoinformatics resources, such as PubChem, PubMed, ClinicalTrials.gov , ChEMBL, SureChEMBL, etc.
- Basic understanding of regulatory agencies and their databases (e.g., the FDA)
- Excellent written and verbal communication abilities with both technical and non-technical audiences, including fluency in English
- Comfort working in a fast-paced, collaborative, start-up environment, working with colleagues and collaborators across disciplines, and tackling novel challenges
- Digitally native, comfortable with social media, software, and new technologies and platforms, and eager to apply new best practices to a growing organization
- Demonstrated ability to pick up new fields of expertise quickly and work with agility in a growth environment
- Candidates with a basic understanding of Python for data processing and automation will be preferred
 Education and Experience 
- A B.S. or M.S. (or equivalent) in organic chemistry, medicinal chemistry, or chemical biology

 Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole.  Anthropic Fellows Program overview 
 The Anthropic Fellows Program is designed to foster AI research and engineering talent. We provide funding and mentorship to promising technical talent - regardless of previous experience.
 Fellows will primarily use external infrastructure (e.g. open-source models, public APIs) to work on project aligned with our research priorities, with the goal of producing a public output (e.g. a paper submission). In one of our earlier cohorts, over 80% of fellows produced papers. We run multiple cohorts of Fellows each year and review applications on a rolling basis.
 Submit your application to the Economics & Policy workstream at the bottom of this page. We are accepting applications on a rolling basis for the next cohort expected to start in January 2027. In some circumstances, we can accommodate fellows starting outside the usual cohort timelines — please note in your application if the January 2027 start date doesn't work for you.
 What to expect 
- 4 months of full-time research 
- Direct mentorship from Anthropic researchers 
- Weekly stipend of 4,615 USD / 3,440 GBP / 6,470 CAD / 4,110 EUR + benefits (these vary by country)
- Substantial funding for compute and other research expenses
 Interview process 
 The interview process will include an initial application, assessments, and interviews. We may ask for references later in the process as well.
 We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work.  Compensation

 Mentors, research areas, & past projects

- Economics

- Peter McCrory

- Marina Favaro
- Jim Baker

- Designing and conducting empirical research on AI's economic effects, drawing on external data sources
- Developing new methodological approaches for studying AI's impact on labor markets, the future of work, and society

- Measuring the extent to which model performance increases with custom harnesses
- Identifying market driven mechanisms that could improve societal resilience to anticipated threats from AI systems
- Identifying which metrics relating to AI R&D could serve as early warning signals for recursive self-improvement

 About Prolific 
 Prolific is not just another player in the AI space – we are building the biggest pool of quality human data in the world.

 We are seeking Director, VP, and C-Level Finance Professionals to join our expert B2B and AI research network. We provide high-level corporate intelligence for global organizations, and we require executive-level insights to validate complex financial data.

 Executive tenure: Proven track record at the Director level or above (CFO, VP, etc.).
- 
 Specialized knowledge: Deep expertise in corporate fiscal strategy, auditing, or financial modeling.

 Professional profile: A verifiable LinkedIn presence or professional history. attention to detail and the ability to concentrate on complex tasks for up to one hour at a time
- 
 A reliable and fast internet connection and access to a computer
- 
 A willingness to self-declare your earnings, as our participants are self-employed
- 
 A Paypal account to receive payment from our clients

 Strategic document audit: Review comprehensive financial reports (200–300 pages) to identify key fiscal drivers.

 B2B validation: Ensure research outputs reflect the practical realities of high-level financial management. willingness to take our skills verification test to assess your suitability for our participant pool

We focus on grounding AI risk management in rigorous analysis, developing policy frameworks that squarely address AGI, advancing technical safety approaches, and fostering global perspectives on durable safety. Through these complementary approaches, CARMA aims to provide critical support to society for managing the outsized risks from advanced AI before they materialize.

title: Senior Finance Consultant: Corporate Strategy & Research - Remote Advisory (Kraków)
description:
Senior Finance Consultant: Corporate Strategy & Research (Remote Advisory)
 About Prolific 
 Prolific is not just another player in the AI space – we are building the biggest pool of quality human data in the world.
 Over 35,000 AI developers, researchers, and organizations use Prolific to gather data from paid study participants with a wide variety of experiences, knowledge, and skills.
 The role 
 We are seeking Director, VP, and C-Level Finance Professionals to join our expert B2B and AI research network. We provide high-level corporate intelligence for global organizations, and we require executive-level insights to validate complex financial data.
Please note: This is an invitation to join our expert talent pool. Participation in specific projects is not guaranteed and is subject to client demand and profile matching.
 Please note, you will be asked to provide your LinkedIn profile URL when joining the waitlist so we can verify your experience.
 Researchers looking for your skills tend to pay up to $100 You must be prepared to complete paid tasks that require one hour of uninterrupted work , though many are shorter.
 What you’ll bring 
- 
 Executive tenure: Proven track record at the Director level or above (CFO, VP, etc.).
- 
 Specialized knowledge: Deep expertise in corporate fiscal strategy, auditing, or financial modeling.
- 
 Professional profile: A verifiable LinkedIn presence or professional history. attention to detail and the ability to concentrate on complex tasks for up to one hour at a time
- 
 A reliable and fast internet connection and access to a computer
- 
 A willingness to self-declare your earnings, as our participants are self-employed
- 
 A Paypal account to receive payment from our clients
 What you’ll be doing in the role 
- 
 Strategic document audit: Review comprehensive financial reports (200–300 pages) to identify key fiscal drivers.
- 
 Executive consulting: Answer nuanced questions regarding corporate finance, risk, and strategy based on provided data.
- 
 B2B validation: Ensure research outputs reflect the practical realities of high-level financial management. willingness to take our skills verification test to assess your suitability for our participant pool
 Why Prolific is a great platform to join as a Participant 
 Joining our platform as a Prolific participant will give you the chance to influence the AI models of the future using professional legal expertise. Once you pass our assessment, you can join Prolific in just 15 minutes, and start enjoying competitive pay rates, flexible hours, and the ability to work from home.
 We've built a unique platform that connects researchers and companies with a global pool of participants, enabling the collection of high-quality, ethically sourced human behavioural data and feedback. This data is the cornerstone of developing more accurate, nuanced, and aligned AI systems.
 We believe that the next leap in AI capabilities won't come solely from scaling existing models, but from integrating diverse human perspectives and behaviours into AI development. By providing this crucial human data infrastructure, Prolific is positioning itself at the forefront of the next wave of AI innovation – one that reflects the breadth and the best of humanity.

title: Associate
description:
About SNV Proximate 
What if you could combine the commercial rigour of consulting, investment, or corporate strategy with the opportunity to create meaningful development impact at scale? SNV’s newly established impact capital accelerator aims to do exactly that: develop commercially viable solutions that generate both business value and development impact. Combining expertise in impact-driven finance and inclusive commercial value chains, SNV Proximate will operate with the pace, ambition, and commercial mindset of a boutique advisory firm while leveraging the reach, credibility, and market presence of a global development organisation.
 Working with companies, investors, development finance institutions, foundations, and governments, this is your chance to join the team that will design, test, and grow new approaches to mobilising investment, strengthening markets, and building more inclusive and resilient value chains across emerging economies. It is a place for people who are excited by building something new, comfortable operating across both commercial and development environments, and motivated by turning ambitious ideas into scalable results.
 Position overview 
SNV is building a commercial markets accelerator, which runs client engagements across two streams — impact-driven finance (IDF) and inclusive commercial value chains (ICVC). Associates are the delivery backbone of both. This role sits at the intersection of substantive client work and internal knowledge building — you will contribute to billable engagements, work directly with clients in the field and in meetings, and help build the evidence base that sharpens the offer over time.
 This is an early-career role designed for someone with 3–5 years of experience who has done solid analytical work and is ready to take on more client-facing responsibility. You will work across both IDF and ICVC engagements, mentored by stream leads, with the expectation that you develop a meaningful specialism in one stream over time.
 The Accelerator is small and the work is varied. In any given month you might be building a financial model for an impact fund client, conducting field interviews with smallholder farmers, drafting a chapter of a market systems report, or packaging an internal case study for BD use. You will not be siloed.
 Who you are 
You are a motivated, curious, and analytical professional who enjoys tackling complex challenges and turning insights into action. You combine strong analytical skills with sound judgement, including knowing when to use AI and when a more human-centred approach is needed.
You thrive in fast-paced environments and enjoy working across different workstreams rather than specialising in a single sector or vertical. Adaptable and commercially minded, you are excited by opportunities to create both business value and development impact.
 As an Associate, you contribute to both winning and delivering client mandates through high-quality analysis, research, stakeholder engagement, and problem-solving. You structure complex problems effectively, identify the key insights and implications, and translate mandates into practical recommendations and deliverables. Your work is accurate, well-reasoned, and thoroughly checked, requiring minimal rework and giving managers confidence in your output.
You act on feedback quickly, keep stakeholders informed, meet deadlines, and proactively flag risks or challenges. Over time, you take on increasingly complex assignments, require less guidance, and build a reputation as a trusted colleague whose expertise and collaboration make clients and peers eager to work with you again.
 Key Responsibilities  
 Client engagement delivery 
- Contribute substantively to client engagements as a core delivery resource — research, analysis, data collection, and drafting, to a standard that requires minimal rework by the delivery lead.
- Conduct primary research: stakeholder interviews, field visits, surveys, and focus groups. Travel to project geographies is a standard part of this role.
 [...] - Build and maintain financial models, data trackers, and analytical frameworks to the level required by the engagement.
 [...] What you bring 
 To be considered for this role, you bring:
- 3–5 years of experience in research, analytical, or advisory role — in consulting, development finance, agribusiness, international development, or a related field.
- Demonstrated experience producing high-quality analytical outputs that were used in client-facing or decision-making contexts.
- Experience conducting primary research — interviews, surveys, or field data collection — in emerging market or development contexts.
- Some exposure to either IDF or ICVC subject matter: impact investing, blended finance, value chain development, agribusiness, or market systems.
- Experience working across multiple projects or workstreams simultaneously.
 Additionally, we value:
- Strong analytical skills — quantitative and qualitative. Comfortable building financial models and analysing large datasets as well as synthesising interview findings and qualitative evidence.
- Clear, concise written English to publication standard. You can write a crisp executive summary, a well-structured analytical section, and a compelling slide — and they do not all sound the same.
- Proficiency with Excel and PowerPoint at a working level. Experience with data analysis tools (R, Python, Stata, or equivalent) an advantage.
- Intellectual curiosity about the sectors we work in. You read beyond the brief.
- English required. French or Portuguese a strong advantage.
- Reporting line: Director
- Location: Flexible. We welcome applications from candidates based anywhere within the time zones spanning Ghana to Singapore. As this role involves international collaboration and travel, candidates should be located within reasonable reach of a well-connected international airport.
 [...]

 Overview

 Fanatics ONE is the loyalty program that recognizes fans across the Fanatics ecosystem. Members earn gifts and access to events they can't buy anywhere else, from seats at sold-out games to Fanatics Fest.
 Every gift campaign and member event has a back office behind it. Someone has to price the tickets, code the expenses, track the invoices and bill other teams when they use what we've paid for. The Department of City Planning (DCP) plans for the future of New York City, working to create thriving and dynamic neighborhoods with access to housing and jobs, resilient infrastructure, and a vibrant public realm. The Department engages communities to develop inclusive plans, expands housing access and economic opportunity, and plans for long-term sustainability.

Department of City Planning offers staff meaningful opportunities to help shape the future of New York City and address some of its most pressing challenges. The Economic Development & Regional Planning Division is charged with supporting the Department of City Planning, City Planning Commission, and City on a wide range of issues related to the equitable economic development of NYC neighborhoods, with a focus on physical development and non-residential space. title: Business Operations Generalist, Finance & Accounting
description:
ABOUT WONDERLY

Wonderly is a closed-loop, end-to-end system that self-improves on our customers’ revenue. We serve the home service industry ($1.3T), and can consistently double a new customer’s revenue within 90 days. We make all of our AI and software completely free - and only get paid when our customers make real money. We’re here helping real small businesses make a life, pay for their children’s college tuition, and live the American dream.

Pre-AI SaaS sold tools. AI companies claim they sell outcomes - task done, call answered, lead booked, ticket resolved - but calls or leads aren’t the outcomes that ultimately matter. Revenue is what ultimately matters, and today, none of the AI companies actually promise revenue. Wonderly changes that.

Our 70-person team (mostly in PDE) spent over a year building in stealth; our thesis is that - if you actually want to control the end result (revenue) of a business and deploy AI fast/cheaply, you can’t just build the sexy part (agents), you must also build the unsexy parts and own everything end to end: the system of record layer and the application layer. We built from scratch every software a home service business needs - replacing ServiceTitan, Squarespace, Ringcentral, Jobber, Square, Hubspot, and a dozen others applications. And we built every agent necessary - AI marketing, AI receptionist, AI voice, AI sales outreach, AI sales coaching, AI follow-ups, AI 3D design, AI finance, AI quoting, AI collections, and more - all embedded inside our own system with native data access. As a result, we can deploy dozens of production-ready Agents to our customers in under 24 hours with no FDEs, no integrations, and no data cleaning work.

We are the most outcome driven business model in the business because we’ve proven our system and AI Agents actually work in driving the end result - revenue. We are not trying to sell our customers a dream - each of our 10+ core AI Agents help improve our customers’ revenue by 5-20%.

Wonderly already has PMF and has gone from 0 → 1 (we are happy to share more over a call), with very clear moat and deep industry knowledge that took a team of 70 hardcore A-players 18 months to build (we are at least 2 years ahead of anyone else in the space). We believe Wonderly has the potential to be a $100B - $1T outcome. The market is massive https://www.acquired.fm/episodes/home-depot: home service businesses across North America (a $1.3T market). We’ve raised over $50M from top-tier investors, have $20M a year in free cashflow from another product line (Motion), and all that money gets pumped into Wonderly.




ABOUT THE HIRING MANAGER

Hi, I’m Harry, Wonderly’s CEO. 

You’ll report directly to me, and you’ll work closely with our CTO, Chander, to build a scalable AI finance & operations system. I’m looking for someone I can trust to own the operational details that keep Wonderly running, from getting the numbers right to working through a vendor contract or fixing a broken process.

You don’t need to have seen every problem before. You do need to ask good questions, exercise sound judgment, and follow through. As you build context and earn trust, you’ll take on more ownership across the business.

 


THE ROLE

We’re hiring someone to own the financial and business operations behind Wonderly.

Accounting is roughly a third of the role. You’ll make sure vendors get paid correctly, coordinate month-end close with our external accountants, and keep tax requirements and financial systems organized. The rest spans contracts, procurement, insurance, equity administration, and the operational problems that come with a growing company.

We want someone with an accounting foundation who wants broad business ownership. You should be comfortable investigating an unfamiliar charge, working through a vendor renewal, coordinating with outside counsel, and building a process so the same issue is easier next time.

Your responsibilities will include:

 - Accounting operations: Validate invoices, collect vendor documentation, coordinate approvals, and schedule payments.
 - Month-end close: Keep close notes, provide supporting information to our accountants, investigate discrepancies, and flag unusual transactions.
 - Tax coordination: Keep filings, registrations, notices, and year-end reporting moving with our external providers.
 - Financial systems: Maintain tools such as Stripe, Subscript, Hubifi, and QuickBooks as the business changes.
 - Contracts and procurement: Coordinate agreements with business owners and counsel, negotiate vendor terms, and track commitments and renewals.
 - Corporate operations: Manage insurance renewals, routine equity administration, corporate records, registrations, and incoming notices.
 - Process improvement: Document recurring work, establish clear owners and deadlines, and work with our internal team to automate repetitive tasks.
You’ll have recurring responsibilities and unexpected problems. You’re accountable for closing the loop on both.
WHAT MAKES THIS ROLE DIFFERENT
You’ll report to our CEO, work closely with our CTO, and see how decisions get made across the company.
 [...] COMPENSATION
 - $100,000–$170,000 total compensation (base + equity), depending on experience.
 - Remote in the US or Canada, with regular in-person gatherings.
Wonderly is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace where everyone is treated with respect and given equal opportunities. We do not discriminate based on gender identity, race, ancestry, disability, religion, sexual orientation, pregnancy status, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. We welcome and encourage all qualified candidates to apply for our job openings.

Location: Midtown Manhattan, New York, NY (In-Person)

 About Eulerity 
 At Eulerity, we are building the future of AI-driven marketing automation. Our platform helps franchises and multi-location businesses manage digital advertising at scale using machine learning, automation, and data.
 As the business scales, we are building the financial infrastructure, data systems, and automated workflows needed to support increasingly complex financial operations.
 We are looking for a Finance Data Analyst Intern who combines an understanding of accounting and finance with strong technical skills. This role is ideal for someone who enjoys working with financial data, building automated workflows, connecting software applications, and developing solutions that improve business processes.
 You will work directly with our Controller and gain hands-on experience across accounting operations, financial reporting, data engineering, and automation.

- Accounting & Finance: Support AP/AR, reconciliations, transaction processing, and month-end close.
- APIs & Integrations: Connect financial and operational systems using APIs, connectors, and integrations.
- Data Pipelines: Build and maintain workflows to extract, transform, validate, and organize financial data.
- Financial Analytics: Use Python, SQL, and Excel to analyze financial data, support reporting, and identify discrepancies.
- Automation & Process Improvement: Develop automated solutions to streamline accounting, reporting, and finance operations.
 What We're Looking For 
 We are looking for candidates with a combination of accounting knowledge, technical capabilities, and analytical thinking. 
 Accounting & Finance Knowledge 
- Understanding of basic accounting principles, including debits and credits, journal entries, reconciliations, and financial statements.
- Coursework, internship experience, or practical exposure to accounting, bookkeeping, or financial analysis.
- Ability to understand financial transactions and how they are recorded and reported.
- Familiarity with QuickBooks Online, Xero, or other accounting systems is a plus.
 Technical Skills – Core Requirement 
- Understanding of APIs and how different software applications communicate.
- Ability to build, configure, or troubleshoot automated workflows and integrations.
- Familiarity with data pipelines and processes involving data extraction, transformation, and validation.
- Proficiency in at least one programming or data tool, such as Python, SQL, JavaScript, or similar.
- Strong proficiency in Excel or Google Sheets.
- Exposure to automation platforms, webhooks, connectors, or AI-powered tools is highly desirable.
 Education 
 We welcome candidates from multiple academic backgrounds, including:
- Accounting and Finance
- Computer Science
- Information Systems / Management Information Systems (MIS)
- Data Analytics / Business Analytics
- Economics or related quantitative fields.
 Candidates pursuing a technology-focused degree with accounting or finance coursework, or a finance/accounting degree with demonstrated programming and automation skills, are particularly encouraged to apply.
 Graduation: December 2027 is preferred; May 2027 or later will also be considered.
 Who You Are 
- Technically Strong: You understand how APIs, software integrations, and automated workflows operate.
- Financially Curious: You understand basic accounting concepts and are interested in how financial systems work.
- Analytical: You enjoy working with data, identifying inconsistencies, and solving problems.
- A Builder: You like developing solutions rather than relying entirely on manual processes.
- Detail-Oriented: You recognize the importance of accuracy in financial reporting and data management.
- Proactive: You take initiative, ask questions, and follow through on assignments.
- Adaptable: You enjoy learning new technologies and working in a fast-paced startup environment.
 What You Will Gain 
- Direct mentorship and exposure to the Controller and Finance team.
- Hands-on experience building financial workflows and automation.
- Practical experience working with APIs, integrations, and data pipelines.
- Exposure to accounting systems, financial reporting, and month-end close.
- Experience working with real financial and operational data in an AI-driven AdTech company.
- An opportunity to contribute to the development of scalable financial infrastructure.

NICE TO HAVE

title: Financial Crimes Analyst
description:
Few people get to build a bank from scratch. Even fewer get to build one at a moment when banking itself is being reinvented.


The Dollar is the best product in the history of the world - there is infinite global demand. But international fintechs and banks are left with two unsatisfying options to choose from: Either build on legacy correspondent banks that are slow and unreliable, or interface with middleware providers that neither move nor hold the dollars directly, but instead rely on underlying legacy banks themselves. At Augustus, we collapse the stack by combining two things: A real, national bank charter (in organization), and Marble, our proprietary core banking system, built around intelligence, made of code.


We are a group of ex-founders, founding employees of unicorns, and people who dropped out of university because they believe this is an industry and career defining opportunity. We are backed with more than $200M from Peter Thiel's Valar Ventures, Tiger Global, Hummingbird, QED, Creandum, and the founders of Nubank, Ramp, Deel, Circle, Fluidstack, Fuse, and Etched.


We are regulated in Europe and live with Euro and Stablecoin clearing today. Now, we are building the US team from the ground up, while continuing to grow rapidly in Europe.




THE ROLE

As a Financial Crimes Analyst at Augustus, you own transaction monitoring end to end, from alert to final disposition. You clear alerts, run case investigations and draft SARs. You find new typologies and turn them into rules.

We’re building an AI native bank, which is designed to run mostly autonomously. Legacy banks scale transaction monitoring with people. We scale it with agents, supporting human decisions. You improve the prompts of our alert review agents, tune monitoring rules to cut false positives, and work with Engineering and Product to automate investigations within our regulatory bounds. Your judgment sets the standard the agents follow. The goal is to make routine alerts disappear so your time goes to the cases that matter.

 


YOUR FIRST SIX MONTHS

 - Months 1-2: Work the queue yourself. Clear transaction monitoring alerts end to end: review, disposition and escalation. Learn the Bank’s TM program and rule logic well enough to see where rules misfire and where the review agents get it wrong.

 - Months 3-4: Own case investigations. Your escalations reach the SAR decision complete and documented, with no rework needed. You recommend rule changes based on false-positive analysis, and you rewrite agent prompts based on what you see in the queue.

 - Months 5-6: Agents handle routine alert disposition. You take complex investigations, SAR drafting and new typologies. You write the case investigation desktop guidance and work with Engineering and Product on the next workflows to automate, within regulatory bounds.

 


WHO WILL THRIVE AT AUGUSTUS

We believe that throwing smart people with high agency at big problems produces the best outcomes. We’re building a modern correspondent bank, and we win by having a better team. The people who succeed here share the following traits:

 - American Dream: You’d rather shoot for gold than settle for mediocrity. You pick the harder goal and stay optimistic when the odds are against you. If it feels easy, we aimed too low.

 - Live Player: You don’t need permission. You rebuild what’s broken without being asked, challenge how things are done, and move before the perfect moment.

 - Ever to Excel: You can’t accept good enough and you take your work personally. When it matters, you do what it takes and keep raising the bar for yourself and your team.

 - Genuine: You play for the company, not your title or turf. Low ego, low drama, no politics. You say it straight, also upwards and always assume good intent.

 

This role is for you if:

 - You reason from first principles. When false positives pile up, you ask which rule needs fixing, not how many analysts to hire.

 - You hunt typologies. When you see a pattern that should have its own rule, you write the requirements and push it into production.
 - You work hard. When alert volume spikes or an investigation gets complex, you stay on it until it’s done right.
 - You challenge how things are done. If a process is slow, redundant or wrong, you say so, also upwards, and you bring the fix.
 - You’re diligent. Your case files are complete, your reasoning is documented, and they hold up when someone checks them.
This is not for you if:
 - You want a fixed checklist and a stable process. Ours changes every time the agents get better.
 - You see automation as a threat to your job. Here it is the job.
 - You treat alert clearing as box-ticking. An examiner may read every disposition you write.
 - You need someone else to tell you a case isn’t good enough.
HARD REQUIREMENTS
 - 2 - 6 years experience. Preferably at a top-tier consultancy (McKinsey, BCG, Bain), a high-bar startup, or as Chief of Staff to a founder.
 - You’ve been promoted or given a bigger scope faster than the standard cycle.
 - You’ve built automations, tools, or workflows that people use today (SQL, scripting, AI tools), not just recommendations.
 - Degree from a top-tier university.
 - Based in New York City and working onsite.
PAY TRANSPARENCY
Compensation packages at Augustus include base salary, equity, and benefits. New hire offers are made based on a candidate's experience, expertise and geographic location. The annual US base salary range for this role is $100,000-$150,000 + equity.

ABOUT THE JOB
The Lead Clinical Research Associate (LCRA) is responsible for providing direction and leadership to the Clinical Research Associate (CRA) team and Clinical Trial Associate (CTA) assigned to studies. The LCRA ensures accurate and timely initiation, enrollment, conduct, completion, and provides project management support. The LCRA ensures adequate study monitoring resources are in place for the study. The LCRA also identifies quality issues related to clinical monitoring activities, and along with the study team, establishes action plans to address them. 


HERE IS WHAT YOU WILL DO:

- Develop, review, and manage clinical plans and guidelines, including the clinical monitoring plan and study timelines; ensure compliance with monitoring intervals according to project requirements, review data reports, CTMS, disseminate listings/reports to study CRAs, and work with CRAs and site staff to resolve data discrepancies
- Create annotated visit report templates and other documents and strategies related to site management and monitoring
- Support training and development of team members, ensure compliance with study specific training requirements, and ensure training is appropriately documented
- Guide and support CRAs, CTAs, and external contract research organizations regarding monitoring, co-monitoring, training, and audit visits; review site visit reports and monitoring letters in accordance with study and SOP requirements
- Manage oversight of the Trial Master File (TMF)/eTMF and assist with filing and quality control
- Track serious adverse events, protocol deviations, enrollment, ICFs, study contacts, investigational supplies, and investigational product for assigned study and review with appropriate members of the study team
- Perform qualification, initiation, interim, and close out visits and provide visit reports as per monitoring guidelines as needed

description:
ABOUT FLUIDSTACK

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it. 


We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.


We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!




HOW WE OPERATE

 - Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

 - Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

 - Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

 - Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

 - Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.




THE PEOPLE TEAM

The People team keeps Fluidstack staffed and compliant as the company scales fast across sites and functions. That includes the people we employ directly and the contractors and vendors who extend our workforce day to day.

Examples of key problems the team is working on

 - Standing up a consistent, compliant process for bringing on and managing contractors across every team and location.

 - Choosing and rolling out the systems that track contractor spend, tenure, and access.

 - Giving hiring managers a clear, fast path to the right workforce solution for their need.
